papers.title: Prediction of lattice thermal conductivity of half-Heusler compounds by machine learning and transfer-function calibration
papers.abstract: High-throughput searches for half-Heusler thermoelectrics increasingly rely on lattice thermal conductivity ($\kappa_L$) from first-principles calculations, or from machine-learning models trained on them. These calculations describe an ideal single crystal, whereas measurements are made on polycrystalline samples, in which grain boundaries and defects scatter heat as well. The resulting gap between calculated and measured $\kappa_L$ has been noted for individual compounds but not, to our knowledge, quantified across a materials class, so the values used for screening carry an unknown, systematic bias. Here we quantify and correct this bias for cubic half-Heusler compounds with 18 valence electrons. Using a curated literature corpus that keeps calculated and measured values apart, we show that calculations overestimate measured $\kappa_L$ in most bonding families, and that the excess shrinks with temperature. Scattering by defects, added to the intrinsic scattering between lattice vibrations, would give such a trend, but the data do not single out one cause. A simple transfer function with this temperature dependence removes the median offset, and refitting its magnitude within a bonding family lowers the median error further, though not consistently compound by compound. Combined with a machine-learning model that predicts the calculated value from crystal structure, and tested on chemistries withheld from all fitting, the method predicts measured $\kappa_L$ in this class about as closely as independent laboratories agree with one another, and provides testable predictions for compounds not yet measured.

papers.title: An explicit Cassels--Tate pairing in characteristic $2$ and the parity of $2$-Selmer ranks
papers.abstract: Let $K$ be a global field of characteristic $2$ and $\varphi\colon E\to E'$ the Verschiebung of an ordinary elliptic curve $E/K$ with a rational point of order $2$. We prove an explicit formula for the homogeneous-space Cassels--Tate pairing on $\Sha(E/K)[\varphi]$ as a sum of local Artin--Schreier symbols, show that it coincides with Kramer's descent pairing and, on $\Sha(E/K)[\varphi]$, with the pairing induced by Milne's flat duality, and deduce that it is non-degenerate on $\Sha(E/K)[\varphi]/\hat\varphi(\Sha(E'/K)[2])$. For every ordinary elliptic curve $A/K$ we express the parity of $\mathrm{rk}\,A(K)+\dim\Sha(A/K)[2]$ by local terms (after Kramer), and identify these with local root numbers at places of semistable or potentially multiplicative reduction, and in further cases using curves with finite $\Sha$. We determine $\Sha$ in examples, and extend the formula to rational points of any prime order $\ell$, the new case being $\ell=\operatorname{char}K$.

papers.title: Suffused NV-FETs for Reconfigurable Hardware
papers.abstract: We define a new category of programmable device, the non-volatile (NV) suffused FET, in response to recent advances in photo- [1]-[3] and e-beam doping [4] We demonstrate that the writing mechanism of suffused NV FETs largely reduces the required access circuitry compared with other NV switches, and that with available configurations as a closed switch, open switch, NFET, or PFET, the suffused NV FET is ideal for configuration storage in reconfigurable arrays, reducing FET count in one case by 84.5%.

authors.name: Thomas Broadfoot
authors.institution: The University of Texas at Dallas

papers.title: Synthetic Surrogate Functional Regression (SSFR): A Robust Framework for Estimating Spatially Varying Covariate Effects in Surrogate-Augmented Neuroimaging
papers.abstract: Relating demographic, clinical, and genetic covariates to high-dimensional imaging outcomes is a core problem in brain imaging, especially when the target modality is observed for only a subset of participants. Generative models can synthesize missing modalities from auxiliary data, but using synthetic images in regression requires care to ensure valid inference. We propose a two-stage Synthetic Surrogate Functional Regression (SSFR) framework for spatially varying covariate effects under partially observed imaging outcomes. By calibrating surrogate information against observed target images, SSFR improves efficiency while remaining robust to discrepancies between the surrogate and target regression functions. We establish consistency and the convergence rate of the estimator, and show that first-stage surrogate-model estimation error does not alter its asymptotic rate. We introduce a voxelwise surrogate explanatory measure $R^2(z)$, the fraction of residual target-image variation explained by a candidate surrogate; with the observation rate, it gives a principled criterion for surrogate screening and indicates the potential efficiency gain. We further develop a weighted bootstrap procedure for simultaneous confidence corridors (SCCs). As surrogate informativeness increases, SCC widths approach those obtained under complete observation, improving localization of significant effects that cannot be identified from the observed data alone. Simulations confirm accuracy and robustness under surrogate misspecification and with surrogates generated by image-to-image neural networks. Applied to spatially normalized PET images from ADNI, SSFR yields interpretable coefficient maps and uniformly narrower SCCs than an analysis using observed PET alone, enlarging the region over which age-related metabolic decline is simultaneously significant.

papers.title: EAGLE: Entity-Aware Grounding with Layered Evidence for High-Resolution Image Understanding
papers.abstract: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) still struggle with fine-grained understanding of high-resolution images: attention heads vary in their reliability for grounding target entities and their attributes, while localized details are often disconnected from the broader scene context. We propose EAGLE (Entity-Aware Grounding with Layered Evidence for High-Resolution Image Understanding), a plug-in framework that jointly selects grounding signals and organizes hierarchical visual evidence. EAGLE employs a fine-grained dataset to screen visually-grounded attention heads, followed by entity-aware grounding to extract target-specific regions. It then integrates hierarchical evidence construction and question-guided routing to select optimal view combinations, feeding them into the frozen MLLM to enhance fine-grained visual understanding. Experiments with Qwen2.5-VL-7B and InternVL3-8B demonstrate that EAGLE consistently improves performance across both backbones and achieves SOTA results on V*, HRBench-4K, and HRBench-8K compared with existing methods using the same backbone.

papers.title: SkillPrivus: Uncovering PRIVacy of USe Harms in Agentic Skills
papers.abstract: Agent skills extend AI assistants through installable instructions and code that can access users' files, accounts, and data. Even when performing their advertised tasks, skills may infer sensitive attributes, retain unnecessary information, or disclose data to unexpected recipients. We study these potential privacy-of-use harms through SkillPrivus, a static audit framework that analyzes skills before installation without executing them. SkillPrivus extracts data operations from code and natural-language instructions, grounds them in source evidence, and adapts Contextual Integrity to assess their appropriateness. Applied to 726 real skills from public marketplaces, 563 of which handle personal data, SkillPrivus flags at least one potential violation in 307 of these skills (54.5%), and its judgments agree with three blind human annotators on 83.2% of resolvable moves. The flagged behaviors include sensitive inferences, information use beyond the stated task, and disclosures to unexpected recipients, suggesting that privacy harms can arise from ordinary skill functionality.

authors.name: Karthikeyan Natesan Ramamurthy

papers.title: SonoAtlasWorld: Anatomy-Grounded Ultrasound World Models for Wide-Range Scanning
papers.abstract: Learning robotic ultrasound policies requires interactive environments for scalable data generation and repeatable evaluation, while exploration on real patients is limited by acquisition costs and safety constraints. Generative world models offer an alternative, but image history and probe actions alone do not ensure anatomical consistency across wide-range scans and changing acoustic windows. We introduce SonoAtlasWorld, an ultrasound world model built on anatomy as state. A persistent 3D anatomical asset extracted from computed tomography (CT) anchors each scan to a specific anatomy. Probe actions determine anatomical and acoustic visibility conditions for a causal ultrasound generator trained on clinical videos. Our three-stage pipeline combines anatomy-conditioned pretraining, causal conversion and long-rollout alignment. Inference optimizations achieve pose-to-ultrasound throughput of 81.2 FPS. To evaluate anatomical control beyond image similarity, we introduce the Action-Following Index (AFI), which measures normalized reconstruction gain over a static-prefix baseline. On 40 held-out 3D volumes, SonoAtlasWorld achieves liver and macro-organ AFI of 0.428 and 0.262, compared with at most 0.117 and 0.038 for the tested action- and geometry-conditioned methods. Long-rollout alignment reduces brightness drift by 3.46x at the end of 40 repeated scan cycles. SonoAtlasWorld also generates offline policy-training demonstrations and supports anatomically grounded closed-loop evaluation. Scaling the generated training data improves key-plane acquisition success from 48.2% to 81.2% on unseen anatomies in simulation, demonstrating its utility for robotic ultrasound policy learning.

papers.title: Determining the Spin and Orbital Period of the Asynchronous Cataclysmic Variable X10 in 47 Tucanae
papers.abstract:
The X-ray source X10 in the globular cluster 47 Tuc has been identified as a cataclysmic variable (CV). With a suggested 4.7 hour periodicity, and a soft X-ray spectrum, it appears to be an unusually X-ray luminous ($L_X=2.2\times10^{32}$ erg s$^{-1}$) polar CV. We use 286 ks of Chandra X-ray Observatory observations of 47 Tuc to study the X-ray timing behavior of 47 Tuc X10. X10 shows clear pulsations in the data, with occasional phase shifts. These suggest that X10 is an asynchronous polar CV, where the spin and orbital periods are slightly misaligned, and the dominant accretion flow shifts from one pole to the other.
  We use a Lomb-Scargle periodogram to suggest potential spin and orbital periods, then model the X-ray lightcurve using simple sinusoids to represent emission from each accretion pole, switching which pole is visible on the beat period. We find a white dwarf spin period of $P_{\mathrm{spin}} = 4.2683$ h and derive an orbital period of $P_{\mathrm{orb}} = 4.6779$ h from the beat modulation. This large degree of asynchronism (8.8%) suggests that X10 is in an unstable equilibrium, and may be a transitional system between an intermediate polar and a fully synchronized polar.

papers.title: Reinforcement Learning Unlearns Corrupted SFT Reasoning
papers.abstract: We show that reinforcement learning (RL) in reasoning tasks can succeed even when the supervised fine-tuning (SFT) data is severely corrupted. In a mathematical reasoning dataset (GSM8K), we systematically corrupt training trajectories across 361 configurations by injecting realistic error types, varying error locations, trace-answer consistency, and corruption ratios up to 100%. While aggregated SFT-only performance steadily deteriorates under corruption (dropping from 43.61% to 13.80%), Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) post-training consistently restores model accuracy back to gold-baseline levels (approximately 60%). Crucially, initializing RL with as few as N = 8 minimal, incorrect, three-line "form-only" traces boosts post-RL performance to 69.30%, outperforming standard gold SFT initialization (60.71%) and GRPO without SFT (35.00%). Further, we show that SFT accuracy is largely uncorrelated with post-RL accuracy (r approximately 0), demonstrating a fundamental asymmetry in post-training: SFT primarily establishes structural layout (form), while RL independently discovers functional reasoning (function).

papers.title: AROMA: Understanding AI Support For Mental Well-being through Role Theory
papers.abstract: AI supporters for mental well-being are becoming more prevalent. When these AI supporters start acting in ways beyond their expected function it leads to relational harm. Standard approaches to evaluating such AI supporters are limited to inspecting their efficacy in narrow task-specific settings, which do not explain these discrepancies in expected and actual behavior. To address this gap, we propose the AROMA (A Role-Oriented Model of Analysis) framework to provide a common role taxonomy for different support contexts. We developed AROMA using a theory-informed annotation of over 7,515 conversations from 13 datasets and propose eight "Role States" based on observed-not prescribed-behavior. We show these Role States vary according to the context of support; depict unique structural and temporal characteristics of AI supporters vis-a-vis Humans; and inform novel AI support prompting strategy for better role alignment. This framework provides a new lens to understand AI support failures.

papers.title: MG-EDA: Maturity-Gated Skew-Normal Estimation of Distribution Algorithms
papers.abstract: Gaussian estimation of distribution algorithms shrink their variance on slopes and stall far from the optimum. This paper equips the corrections that act along the direction of movement -- a mean shift, an elongation of the covariance along the path and a skewness -- with the rule they lack: a calibrated gate, driven by a maturity statistic of the population, decides whether, how strongly and for how long each correction acts, and when the gate is closed the algorithm is exactly the estimation of multivariate normal algorithm (EMNA). The statistic is a cumulative path of whitened mean shifts with an inverse-Wishart correction, whose expectation is one under a null model without systematic movement and whose quantiles give thresholds with known false-alarm rate. It gates the three corrections as three rank-one terms of one matrix sampling equation, the skewness being carried by a skew-normal sampler that preserves the estimated mean and covariance; all vanish at maturity. We call the resulting algorithm the maturity-gated EDA (MG-EDA). A full factorial study on a training set of black-box optimization benchmarking (BBOB) functions separates the parameters: variance scaling is the prerequisite, the mean shift needs a feedback correction removing the injected shift from the statistic, the elongation turns the variance loss on a slope into a gain, and the skewness substitutes for the mean shift rather than complementing it. On held-out instances MG-EDA with the first- and second-order corrections is significantly better than the skewness-only predecessor and than EMNA with variance scaling, ties with EMNA with anticipated mean shift, and trails the adapted maximum-likelihood Gaussian model (AMaLGaM) in 20 dimensions.

papers.title: Mode Recommendation and Dynamic Routing Guidance for Improved Trip Quality in Mixed Traffic Networks
papers.abstract: Urban mixed traffic networks provide diverse mobility options, yet conventional routing guidance with fixed travel modes leaves the benefits of coordinating travel modes and route planning largely unexploited. This paper proposes an integrated mode recommendation and dynamic routing guidance framework for urban mixed traffic networks comprising private vehicles, autonomous vehicles, and buses. We formulate a dynamic trip index (DTX) that incorporates mode-specific travel time, monetary cost, and convenience, enabling consistent evaluation of trip quality across travel modes. Using this measure, we develop a mode recommendation method that selects feasible autonomous vehicle or bus services based on predicted DTX for travelers without private vehicles, while preserving service capacity for travelers with known demand. We integrate this method with dynamic routing guidance for private and autonomous vehicles to improve the average trip quality of all travelers. Simulation studies involving $1{,}500$ travelers on a real-world road network in Shanghai, China, show that the proposed framework increases the mean realized DTX by $13.01\%$ compared with dynamic routing guidance alone and by $19.68\%$ compared with fixed travel modes with preplanned routes, highlighting the value of mode flexibility in improving trip quality beyond route adaptation.

papers.title: Recursive Relations for Categorified Young Symmetrizers in Type $\mathbb{B}$
papers.abstract: The category of bounded-above chain complexes of Soergel bimodules of any finite type $\mathbb{X}_n$ contains a symmetrizer complex $\mathbf{P}_{\mathbb{X}_n}$ which kills non-identity Soergel bimodules up to homotopy. It has been shown in previous work that, in type $\mathbb{A}$, $\mathbf{P}_{\mathbb{A}_{n+1}}$ can be obtained as a semi-infinite extension between copies of $\mathbf{P}_{\mathbb{A}_n}$ and its product with a Jucys-Murphy complex. We prove an analogous recursion holds between the symmetrizers for type $\mathbb{B}_n$ and $\mathbb{B}_{n+1}$. Following the method of the result in type $\mathbb{A}$, we then use this to prove that the cohomology ring of the endomorphism algebra of $\mathbf{P}_{\mathbb{B}_n}$ is a polynomial ring.

papers.title: TrajRealm: A Large-Scale Point Tracking Dataset with Diverse Dynamics
papers.abstract: General-purpose point tracking requires large-scale training data with diverse dynamics, yet existing datasets struggle to combine rich dynamic content, accurate scene geometry, and sufficient scale. We introduce TrajRealm, the first public synthetic point-tracking dataset to reach the ten-million-frame scale, constructed from games and embodied simulations. TrajRealm uses the rich environments and motion systems of modern games to capture diverse targets, activities, and interactions across diverse worlds, while embodied simulations add robot manipulation and indoor navigation data. The dataset provides RGB observations, depth, camera parameters, and persistent 2D and 3D point trajectories. These annotations provide precise, geometrically consistent supervision across foreground objects and static environmental surfaces. We also build TrajRealm-Bench with eight subcategories under Interaction and Locomotion to evaluate tracking across diverse scenes. Benchmark evaluations reveal the strengths and limitations of existing trackers in handling complex motion and maintaining long-term point correspondences. Training on TrajRealm improves the performance of existing tracking methods on synthetic and real-world benchmarks.

papers.title: ECG-LabWAS: A Laboratory-Wide Association Study Using a Fine-Tuned Single-Lead Electrocardiogram Foundation Model
papers.abstract: Laboratory testing guides clinical diagnosis but requires blood sampling and processing. The electrocardiogram (ECG) is fast and noninvasive and may carry information about laboratory abnormalities, yet most AI-ECG models target one test at a time using 12-lead recordings. We conducted an exploratory ECG laboratory-wide association study (ECG-LabWAS), fine-tuning an ECG foundation model pretrained on 10.8 million ECGs to screen 50 laboratory tests from single-lead waveforms alone. The model was developed in an emergency-department cohort (MC-MED; 31,826 patients) and applied unchanged to an independent hospital cohort (MIMIC-IV; 115,921 patients). Of 89 abnormality directions (low or high values of each test), 33 met the same screening criteria in both cohorts. Areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve in the two cohorts were 0.841 and 0.838 for elevated NT-proBNP, 0.769 and 0.740 for elevated cardiac troponin, 0.755 and 0.731 for elevated creatinine, and 0.713 and 0.710 for low potassium. Discrimination changed little when the ECG--laboratory matching window was widened from $\pm$1 to $\pm$24 hours. Model predictions reproduced the co-occurrence of observed abnormalities but were about twice as tightly coupled, largely along one shared component consistent with overall illness severity; low potassium, elevated NT-proBNP and troponin, and markers of renal function retained discrimination beyond that of correlated tests. In exploratory analyses, ECG-assisted versions of the modified Glasgow Prognostic Score and the systemic inflammatory response syndrome criteria were associated with in-hospital and one-year mortality. These results identify which laboratory abnormalities warrant analyte-specific study with single-lead ECG.

papers.title: Baryon-Enhanced Strong Lensing Signatures of Self-Interacting Dark Matter Subhalos
papers.abstract: Self-interacting dark matter (SIDM) is generally expected to suppress subhalo strong lensing through core formation, with subsequent gravothermal collapse potentially enhancing it. We show that compact stars can make a viable population of galaxy-hosting SIDM subhalos more efficient lenses than their cold dark matter (CDM) counterparts. When the baryonic potential weakens or reverses the inner velocity-dispersion gradient, SIDM halos suppress or bypass core formation, allowing inner densities to grow from early times. The evolved SIDM subhalos produce larger deflection angles and tangential caustics than in CDM. Such galaxy-hosting subhalos also dominate the galaxy-galaxy strong-lensing (GGSL) budget in clusters, yet lie far below the resolution of cosmological simulations. We calibrate a baryonic parametric SIDM model to predict their effects in the three most massive TNG300-1 clusters, finding GGSL cross sections 1.4--2.7 times those in CDM, comparable to the excess inferred in recent analyses. Baryon-enhanced SIDM lensing can thus account for the observed GGSL excess and predicts stronger perturbations from luminous satellites, testable through resolved distortions of background arcs and rings.

authors.name: Siyuan Hou
authors.institution: Merck & Co., Inc., Rahway, NJ, USA (United States)

papers.title: Semiparametric Efficiency for Entropic Optimal Transport under Structured Distribution Shift
papers.abstract: Can structural information improve estimation of entropic optimal transport (EOT), and when is the gain zero? We study a fixed-dimensional exponential density ratio model (DRM) with a nonparametric baseline, compact support, and fixed positive regularization. At positive limiting sampling fractions, an exact projection identity quantifies the variance gain from the restriction. The pooled empirical-likelihood estimator attains the restricted bound and supports asymptotically valid confidence intervals when the bound is positive. Even under correct specification, the gain can be zero and can shrink as the tilt space expands. The same projection residual determines direction-specific first-order bias under local misspecification. When both samples grow and the target fraction vanishes, a zero first-order tilt derivative can leave source fluctuations and quadratic tilt error as the leading terms. Their balance gives a phase transition in the limiting distribution. A continuous example gives different convergence rates for two correctly specified bases at the same distribution pair. Controlled experiments assess the fixed-proportion theory. Natural-data comparisons distinguish variance reductions from improvements in reference RMSE driven by smaller reference bias.

authors.institution: University of Science and Technology of China

papers.title: EgoLAM: Learning Latent Actions from Hand and Head Motion
papers.abstract: Latent action models let a robot policy learn from video by turning the change between two frames into a training target. In egocentric video, a cup can move across the image because a hand pushes it or because the wearer turns. Both changes help predict the next frame, but only the first describes manipulation. During training, EgoLAM supervises the action code with measured wrist motion and supplies camera motion separately to the forward model. Even when the wearer turns while pushing a cup, the training target still describes how the hand pushed it. The action encoder pools object slots around each hand, and wrist translation and rotation can be decoded from the code in a common reference frame. Extracting a code then requires only two RGB frames. Alongside LARYBench classification and regression, we measure how much wrist motion a frozen code retains and how strongly it responds to a synthetic view or lighting change. EgoLAM has the highest hand-motion decoding score among eight evaluated models. Across three LIBERO suites, policies pretrained on its codes and fine-tuned on expert demonstrations achieve 79.38% mean success, 28.73 points above expert behavior cloning and 9.76 points above the strongest other latent action model in each suite on average.

papers.title: PanoUAV-Track: Full-Spherical UAV Visual Tracking in the Wild
papers.abstract: Existing UAV tracking benchmarks predominantly rely on perspective cameras with limited fields of view. Omnidirectional cameras enable full-spherical observation, yet tracking from moving UAV platforms remains largely unexplored. Unlike ground-level panoramic tracking, UAV-mounted omnidirectional cameras observe targets across both azimuth and elevation, introducing geometric challenges under equirectangular projection (ERP). To investigate this setting, we capture approximately \textbf{40 hours of real-world 8K panoramic UAV video} and construct \textbf{PanoUAV-Track} through temporal clip extraction, target annotation, and the integration of simulated sequences. The resulting benchmark comprises 1,895 sequences, 507,961 frames, and 2,872 annotated objects, covering real-world daytime and nighttime scenes alongside simulation, and supporting both visual and language-based target specification. Through extensive evaluations, we reveal a clear \textbf{perspective-to-spherical} generalization gap and identify tracking degradation associated with latitude-dependent distortion and ERP seam discontinuity. To address these challenges, we propose \textbf{PanoUAV-Tracker (PUTrack)}, a geometry-aware tracking framework combining latitude-adaptive search and seam-aware periodic sampling. PUTrack improves zero-shot and in-domain tracking, particularly for seam-crossing targets. Code and benchmark resources will be available\footnote{\textcolor{tabpink}{https://libingyu01.github.io/PanoUAV-Track/}}.

authors.name: Lichang Yang
authors.institution: University of Electronic Science and Technology of China

authors.name: Junyu Gao
authors.institution: University of Science and Technology Liaoning

papers.title: ROSWORLD: When Digital Task Competence Meets Physical Execution
papers.abstract: Computer-use agents now solve most desktop tasks through direct software input, but a robot using the same computer must turn GUI knowledge into physical contact with a keyboard and mouse. We introduce ROSWorld, a benchmark that couples a physically simulated robot workstation to a live OSWorld desktop, so that a robot and a desktop agent pursue the same goals under the same official evaluators. The evaluated model receives observations only from the workstation camera views and operates the peripherals through either a single-arm rigid probe or dual-arm dexterous hands. Across five frontier models and 40 tasks in ten applications, models that complete 31-39 tasks on the desktop complete at most 23 with the probe and 28 with the hands. Paired trajectory analysis shows that models adapt their interaction strategies toward keyboard input, yet physical execution frequently fails through missed presses, incorrect targets, and unintended contacts. ROSWorld makes the gap between knowing what to do on a computer and physically doing it measurable.

authors.name: Xuehui Wang
authors.institution: University of Chinese Academy of Sciences

authors.name: Jiaqi Wang
authors.institution: Harbin University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Trained on Harm, Still Refusing: A Training-Time Defense for Code Generation
papers.abstract: Fine-tuning enables safety-aligned code language models to adapt to diverse downstream tasks. However, training on untrusted data can severely undermine their ability to refuse harmful requests. Notably, we find that models comply with harmful requests even though harmfulness information remains highly decodable from their internal representations. Moreover, an initial preference for refusal does not necessarily translate into sustained refusal behavior throughout generation. Together, these findings reveal a critical gap between recognizing harmful requests and consistently refusing to fulfill them. To address this gap, we introduce SAFEHOLD, a novel provider-enforced defense framework that preserves safety alignment during harmful fine-tuning by treating refusal as a sustained generation process rather than a single response decision. Specifically, SAFEHOLD preserves the aligned model's full-vocabulary response distribution at the initial generation position through decision-boundary anchoring, while supervising the complete refusal sequence through refusal-path reinforcement. We conduct extensive experiments evaluating safety, utility, and internal mechanisms. SAFEHOLD reduces average ASR by 72.03 percentage points relative to undefended fine-tuning, outperforming five SOTA defenses by 24.32 to 70.87 percentage points. Meanwhile, it improves average HumanEval pass@1 by 10.24 percentage points over undefended fine-tuning, while maintaining an average XSTest over-refusal rate of only 2.73 percent. Overall, these results demonstrate that SAFEHOLD effectively mitigates safety degradation during harmful fine-tuning while preserving benign-task utility.

papers.title: Too Fast to Doubt? Skipping Reasoning Leaves Jev-like Models Vulnerable
papers.abstract: Fast decision models offer low-latency actions and explicit confidence estimates. We audit four state-of-the-art decision models on 1,440 paired synthetic browser tasks, injecting false conclusions or evidence interpretations through external comments. Across models, clean accuracy averages 91.0%, yet two-shot attack success reaches 81.2%. Mean expected calibration error rises from 2.6% on clean inputs to 36.7% under conclusion poisoning and 36.1% under evidence poisoning. Clean accuracy and calibration therefore do not ensure reliable decisions under injection. We further compare GPT-6 Luna and Luna Decisions, which share the same base model, on 48 matched tasks. With a chain of thought averaging fewer than 30 reasoning tokens per response, low-effort GPT-6 Luna answers 95.83% of poisoned inputs correctly, versus 38.54% for native Luna Decisions, while mean selected-generation latency increases from 0.29 to 1.94 seconds. These results expose a sharp latency-robustness trade-off: skipping reasoning for sub-second speed leaves fast decision models substantially more vulnerable to deceptive web content.

authors.name: Xiao Li
authors.institution: Southwest University of Science and Technology

papers.title: When Are Images Needed in Multimodal Machine Translation? Text-Only Routing for On-Demand Visual Context
papers.abstract: Image-guided multimodal machine translation (MMT) leverages visual context to resolve translation-relevant uncertainty. However, prevailing systems either process images unconditionally or apply gating only after visual encoding, leaving redundant visual computation unavoidable. To mitigate this computational overhead, routing decisions must rely on a pre-visual source signal. Crucially, surface-level ambiguity does not equate to visual dependence, as intra-sentence textual context often suffices for disambiguation. We therefore formulate visual invocation as source-text sufficiency prediction: determining exclusively from the source text whether translation-relevant uncertainty remains unresolved. To support this formulation, we construct a visual-dependency dataset with three fine-grained labels (no_ambiguity, text_resolved, and vision_needed) and verify discriminative visual evidence for vision_needed instances. We further propose PreVIR, a lightweight, backend-agnostic text-only router that selects between text-only and multimodal branches before computing visual features. Experiments on English-to-Chinese MMT demonstrate that PreVIR achieves a favorable COMET-budget trade-off relative to strong routing baselines. At its default operating point, it substantially reduces visual calls while maintaining translation quality comparable to always-on multimodal inference. Label-wise and case analyses show that this trade-off stems from distinguishing genuine visual dependency from contextually resolved ambiguity.

papers.title: Finite-Time Singularity Formation for the Three-Dimensional Euler Equations
papers.abstract: We construct smooth periodic initial data for the three-dimensional incompressible Euler equations whose solution blows up in finite time. The velocity remains bounded, while the vorticity magnitude at the origin tends to infinity. Away from the origin, the velocity and its time derivative have smooth spatial limits at the singular time. The construction uses localized Craik--Criminale waves as building blocks of a multi-scale construction.

papers.title: SecretAgent: A Multi-Agent Framework for Privacy Protection against Vision Language Models
papers.abstract: Vision-language models (VLMs) can infer private information from shared images, including locations, personally identifiable information (PII), and personal attributes such as age and sex, even from medical images. Adversarial perturbations can protect such information against black-box VLMs, but existing methods overlook image quality and introduce visible artifacts into the images they protect. We present SecretAgent, the first general multi-agent framework that protects image privacy against VLMs while preserving visual fidelity. LLM agents iteratively locate the visual evidence that reveals private information and adapt an invisible perturbation to the target VLM's answers and to an appearance reviewer agent, which rejects any candidate with visible artifacts. We instantiate SecretAgent with two complementary variants: SecretAgent-Gradient optimizes the perturbation through six surrogate encoders for cross-model transferability, and the gradient-free SecretAgent-Tool composes procedural noise and achieves the best perceptual fidelity on three of the five datasets. Experiments on four privacy applications (geolocation, PII, facial, and medical) across five datasets and six VLMs show that SecretAgent preserves image quality substantially better than existing methods while achieving state-of-the-art privacy protection in every application, and that its protection transfers to other VLMs.

authors.name: Mengyu Wang
authors.institution: Xi'an University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Counterexamples to a conjecture of Gao and Gu on weighted Catalan numbers
papers.abstract: We construct infinitely many counterexamples to a conjecture of Gao and Gu on when the 2-adic valuations of weighted Catalan numbers equal those of Catalan numbers.

papers.title: From Letter-of-Credit Requirements to Executable Specifications: Evaluating Verification Accuracy and Completeness
papers.abstract: In letter-of-credit (LC) document examination, a correct final decision does not show that every requirement was examined. We therefore evaluate examination requirement by requirement and make each requirement executable. A language model converts the bill of lading (BL) and commercial invoice (IV) requirements of a credit into atomic conditions and logical structures, and a deterministic verifier retrieves the named evidence and computes each outcome, so every check can be compared with a gold encoding and traced to logged evidence. Because LC records are confidential, our on-premises 9B parser is fine-tuned only on synthetic pairs built from templates and human-reviewed public document values. On 345 real LC cases, final-decision accuracy proves misleading: a constant PASS rule has the highest raw accuracy while examining nothing. Although it never sees a real record during training, the fine-tuned parser detects 93% of the atomic requirements its ontology covers and reconstructs 86% of the covered requirements exactly. It verifies 82% of the evaluable requirements correctly, against 54% for a tool-using agent, and leads the agent on both satisfied requirements and discrepancies. It also completely examines 1.8 times as many cases as few-shot prompting of the same model, while direct prediction and the agent complete none. Executing the gold encodings with the same verifier shows that some of the remaining errors, missed discrepancies included, come from the operators and normalization, which a better parser alone cannot fix. Every rejection comes with a trace of the units and evidence behind it, which suits examiner-in-the-loop review.

papers.title: Real-Time On-Drone Hyperspectral Anomaly Detection for Wilderness Search and Rescue
papers.abstract: Wilderness search-and-rescue (WSAR) teams use uncrewed aerial systems (UASs) to survey terrain for indicators of missing persons that are rare, blend into the background, or lack thermal signatures. Hyperspectral imaging (HSI) provides rich spectral information, but its high data volume challenges real-time on-drone processing. We present SABL, an edge-computing pipeline for on-drone Spectral Anomaly-Based Localization. SABL integrates hyperspectral streaming with exponentially moving Reed-Xiaoli (ERX) anomaly detection and DBSCAN spatial filtering to group pixel-level anomalies into candidate search regions. SABL is evaluated on data collected during a 10-day deployment with Quinhagak Search and Rescue (QSAR) in remote Alaska. It processes hyperspectral scanlines at 5.67-5.73 ms per line, meeting the camera's 10-ms acquisition interval; DBSCAN requires only 6.5-12.5 ms per 100-line update for filtering. SABL achieves approximately 56% and 99% object-level precision on QSAR-selected search indicators across two scenes, with corresponding recall of 55% and 29%, providing significant background filtering while identifying difficult-to-see anomalous search indicators.

papers.title: Do Senior Agents Do Their Job? Measuring Role Integrity in How LLM Agents Use Subordinate Material
papers.abstract: Multi-agent LLM systems increasingly divide long tasks among subagents whose reports a senior agent turns into the final answer. Such a division of labor pays off only if each agent, and above all the senior agent, carries out the duties of its role. Current evaluations, however, mostly score the final answer, and a fluent, well-cited answer cannot show whether the senior agent weighed its subagents' reports or merely aggregated them. To assess whether a senior agent meets its assigned responsibilities, we define role integrity as the preservation of an agent's functional responsibilities when it acts on its subordinates' material. To measure it, we introduce RI-Bench, a behavioral benchmark grounded in the structures and public records of three institutional hierarchies: peer review, appellate adjudication, and parliamentary inquiry. We choose these hierarchies because their rules explicitly assign the senior role a duty toward subordinate material, and together they cover three basic duties: to weigh, to verify, and to relay. Rather than scoring output correctness, we measure how senior agents' outputs respond to controlled changes in subordinate material, using rule-based checks and a rubric-guided LLM judge calibrated against human annotation. Across eight LLMs and over 12,000 agentic episodes, senior agents rarely adopt a planted procedural error (2.9% of rulings) but often follow a majority of generic reviews (up to 71% of decisions) or drop witnesses' stated limitations (up to 65% of cited claims). Obligation prompts reduce these failures without removing them, and they also shift behavior in the control conditions. These findings motivate direct, obligation-specific evaluation of role integrity rather than inferring it from general capability or explicit role instructions. Code and data are available at https://github.com/jxtse/ri-bench.

authors.name: Changjiang Jiang
authors.institution: Chongqing University of Posts and Telecommunications

papers.title: Tripwire: Robot Agents that Program Their Own Interrupts under Human Disturbance
papers.abstract: Agent harnesses are turn-based: the agent acts, waits for the result, then reasons. When the action invokes a pretrained robot policy, such as a vision-language-action (VLA) or world action model (WAM), the policy may react continuously to observations, but the agent cannot revisit its decision until the call returns. Meanwhile, a person may step into the robot's path or move the object it is about to grasp. Invoking the agent more often narrows this blind interval, but a reasoning model takes seconds per decision and most control steps need no new one. We propose TRIP, a training-free, event-driven harness in which the agent programs its own interrupts. With each call, the agent writes a tripwire: a lightweight, stateful Python program that runs alongside the policy, can query a compact VLM (for example, to locate a person and measure their distance), and decides whether the call continues or control returns to the agent. When it fires, the harness halts the policy and returns control with the reason; the agent then reassesses, adapts, and continues under a rewritten tripwire. We evaluate TRIP with three VLAs and one WAM on RoboHD, a benchmark of 168 RoboCasa365 scenes in which a simulated person disturbs the robot and any human-robot contact counts as failure. Compared with a turn-based harness using the same agent and tools, TRIP halves the rate of human contact with the strongest policy, raising safety from 61.3% to 81.3%, without sacrificing task success (38.7% vs. 31.0%). Real-robot experiments show that TRIP completes two manipulation tasks under human interference where the turn-based harness and the policy alone largely fail.

papers.title: DepthMSA: Combinatorial Training and Budget-Aware Depth Allocation for Multimodal Sentiment Analysis
papers.abstract: State-of-the-art multimodal sentiment analysis (MSA) models rely on large pretrained encoders, yet typically process every modality to its full depth, regardless of its computational cost or predictive contribution. This raises a fundamental question: how should limited computation be allocated across modalities to preserve predictive performance? We reveal a substantial mismatch between the computational cost of modality encoders and the predictive benefit of processing them more deeply, suggesting that different modalities require different encoding depths. However, enabling heterogeneous depths introduces a key challenge: representations extracted at different depths must still be effectively fused. To address this, we propose $\textbf{DepthMSA}$, a budget-aware framework that supports flexible modality depths within a single MSA model. Specifically, we introduce combinatorial anytime training, which supervises the fusion head across all cross-modal depth combinations using a single full-depth encoder pass. At inference, a training-free, cost-aware allocator selects the configuration with the lowest validation-calibrated error under a sample-specific FLOPs budget. On CMU-MOSEI, DepthMSA maintains accuracy within one percentage point of the full-depth model while reducing measured FLOPs by 45\%, or by 82\% with a separately trained skip-enabled variant. When a CLIP visual encoder dominates computation, the allocation shifts toward reducing visual depth, achieving 56\% fewer FLOPs at unchanged accuracy. Compared with ADMN, an adaptive layer-allocation method that trains a controller for each budget, the skip-enabled variant reaches its accuracy with 3.2$\times$ fewer FLOPs and lower latency, without any per-budget training. Our project is available at https://pwang322.github.io/DepthMSA/.

authors.name: Jie Peng
authors.institution: University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill

papers.title: Tight Probabilistic Aspects of Friends-and-Strangers Graphs
papers.abstract:
Friends-and-strangers graphs, introduced by Defant and Kravitz, model arrangements of people on positions. We consider two graphs $X$ and $Y$ on $n$ vertices. The vertices of $X$ represent positions with edges denoting adjacencies while the vertices of $Y$ represent people with edges denoting friendships. Their \emph{friends-and-strangers graph} is denoted by $\mathsf{FS}(X,Y)$. Its vertices are all one-to-one placements of people on positions, and two placements are adjacent if one can swap two friends on adjacent positions to get from one placement to the other.
  A fundamental question is whether or not a friends-and-strangers graph is connected. A natural probabilistic analog is ``If $X$ and $Y$ are independently sampled Erd\H{o}s--R\'{e}nyi graphs with $n$ vertices and edge probability $p,$ what is the threshold probability for $\mathsf{FS}(X,Y)$ to be connected with high probability?'' Alon, Defant, and Kravitz (2023) showed that $p = n^{-1/2+o(1)}$ is the threshold probability and conjectured that $p = \Theta(n^{-1/2}).$ Milojevi\'{c} (2024) disproved this by showing $p = \Omega(n^{-1/2}\sqrt{\log n})$ is necessary for connectivity with high probability. In this work, we prove a matching upper bound, thus establishing that the threshold is $p = \Theta(n^{-1/2}\sqrt{\log n}).$

papers.title: Proactive Defense Benchmark against Deepfake Generation
papers.abstract: Despite the proliferation of proactive defenses against deepfakes, the lack of a unified evaluation protocol precludes fair comparison and masks critical vulnerabilities. To bridge this gap, we present the first comprehensive benchmark that systematically assesses disruption, robustness, and transferability encompassing pixel, perceptual, and identity metrics. Our extensive analysis reveals that fidelity and identity metrics capture orthogonal performance axes, often leading to conflicting interpretations when relied upon individually. Furthermore, we identify a fundamental trade-off where peak white-box performance signals overfitting, and we introduce a calibrated evaluation to correct generator-induced identity bias. By exposing these blind spots, we establish a rigorous standard to guide the development of genuinely generalizable protections. Project page is available at: https://proactivedefensebenchmark.github.io/

authors.name: Joonhyuk Baek
authors.institution: MIT Computer Science and Artificial Intelligence Laboratory

authors.name: Wonjune Seo
authors.institution: Ulsan National Institute of Science and Technology

papers.title: ReSA: Preserving Reference-Specified Foreground in In-Context Segmentation
papers.abstract: In-context segmentation uses annotated references to specify the target and its extent in a query image. Accurately transferring this reference-specified foreground requires recovering target regions while suppressing irrelevant predictions. We propose ReSA, a reference-guided framework that unifies query adaptation and mask selection through a shared reference kernel. ReSA leverages foreground and background reference prototypes to constrain prediction changes during adaptation and guide foreground selection through reference-weighted reconstruction. This shared guidance promotes consistent use of reference information across prediction refinement and mask formation. ReSA further selects among adapted predictions and aligns boundary refinement with the selected foreground threshold. We establish a theoretical bound connecting reference-response changes during adaptation and soft reconstruction. With a frozen visual encoder and lightweight test-time adaptation, ReSA requires no offline task training. Ablation studies demonstrate improved foreground retention and effective suppression of false-positive regions, while qualitative results show more complete masks with fewer isolated artifacts. Across ten object, part, and cross-domain segmentation benchmarks, ReSA achieves the highest average mIoU among the evaluated methods, reaching 62.6% in 1-shot and 71.8% in 5-shot.

papers.title: Open CDLM: A Benchmark and Library for Continuous Diffusion Language Models
papers.abstract: Reliable comparisons of continuous diffusion language models (CDLMs) require evaluating both model fit and the distribution of generated text. Two common practices leave this goal only partially addressed. Likelihood-based evaluation often reports a variational upper bound on discrete negative log-likelihood, whose slack can confound comparisons. Generated-sample-based evaluation commonly combines generative perplexity with within-sequence unigram entropy; both scores can remain favorable even when a sampler produces the same text on every draw. We introduce \textbf{Open CDLM}, a benchmark for evaluating CDLMs and their samplers, and describe the design of an accompanying open-source library to support reproducible comparisons. For likelihood-based evaluation, we clarify which comparisons of model fit are supported by reported perplexity bounds and how those conclusions depend on the evaluation procedure. For sample-based evaluation, we use \textit{Kernel Text Discrepancy} (\textbf{KTD}) to compare collections of generated and real texts, alongside diagnostics for diversity, validity, and coverage. In controlled OpenWebText experiments, replacing a collection of texts with copies of a single selected passage improves both conventional generation scores. MAUVE detects the resulting collapse, and its response to other perturbations depends on the text representation and the type of perturbation. This work marks the beginning of Open CDLM as an open-source project for CDLM research. We will maintain and extend the library over time and welcome contributions from the community.

authors.name: Jiayi Han
authors.institution: Second Affiliated Hospital of Xi'an Jiaotong University

papers.title: Closed-loop policy optimisation for cylinder wake control via differentiable simulation
papers.abstract: Suppressing vortex shedding behind a circular cylinder is a classical problem in active flow control.Model-free deep reinforcement learning (DRL) learns such policies by interacting with the flow without differentiating its dynamics, which typically requires a large interaction budget. This study optimises closed-loop policies by differentiable simulation: control-loss gradients propagate through the simulated flow to the policy parameters, which are updated by reverse-mode automatic differentiation. The policy maps local velocity measurements to a jet amplitude imposed through differentiable synthetic-jet boundary conditions. In a two-dimensional confined cylinder wake at Rey=100, eight policy updates (about 78 shedding periods of forward simulation) give approximately 8% drag reduction and 99.6% suppression of lift fluctuations, the drag level being comparable to reported DRL results. Suppression is sustained by feedback: a mean-matched constant jet does not maintain it, whereas the same policy responds similarly at three activation phases and recovers after upstream disturbances. A velocity-deviation reward alone retains strong suppression, and observations of two instantaneous velocity components at one near-wake or surface location reach about 99.8% suppression, whereas a single surface pressure leaves residual oscillations. Together with related DRL results, this suggests that reward and observation requirements here are set by policy optimisation and flow physics.

authors.name: Yulin Xie
authors.institution: Key Laboratory on Development and Application of Rural Renewable Energy

papers.title: To Own or Not to Own? Endogenous Ownership in Peer-to-Peer Sharing of Private Autonomous Vehicles
papers.abstract: Autonomous driving allows private owners to release their vehicles to an on-demand platform and earn income when they do not need them. This possibility changes vehicle acquisition incentives, as rental income can encourage purchases, while access to shared vehicles can reduce the need for personal ownership. Understanding these competing effects is essential to assessing the ownership implications of private AVs sharing. While existing models of private AV sharing often take ownership as given, in this paper, we develop a stationary equilibrium model in which vehicle ownership and listing decisions determine service availability and operational frictions, which in turn shape individuals' incentives to own and share. Based on the model, we first characterize individual choices by comparing payoffs of being an owner and a non-owner. We then analyze the resulting potential population partitions, establish conditions for the existence of an active sharing market, and categorize them by owner types. The equilibrium is presented by a system of equations and solved through a tailored algorithm. An illustrative numerical study on calibrated U.S. travel and vehicle cost data shows that sharing can either increase or decrease ownership, depending on the balance between purchases encouraged by rental income and ownership displaced by shared vehicles. The balance is shaped by market parameters, including market density, AV cost, and platform operating conditions. Platform pricing and municipal regulation can also influence ownership through their effects on acquisition incentives and the shared service that makes nonownership attractive. These findings highlight the range of possible ownership outcomes in private AV sharing markets, and the model provides a framework for evaluating how market conditions, platform decisions, and regulation shape these outcomes.

papers.title: Geometrically Constrained Learning II: Agnostic Proper Learning of Lipschitz Functions
papers.abstract:
We give a proper learner for Lipschitz functions over the Gaussian distribution on $\mathbb{R}^d$. Given random Gaussian examples labeled by a $\lambda$-Lipschitz function, $\lambda \ge 1$, the learner returns a function $h:\mathbb{R}^d\to\mathbb{R}$ that is globally $\lambda$-Lipschitz and has loss (absolute or squared) at most $\varepsilon$. The sample complexity, running time, and representation size are \[
  (d+1)^{\mathsf{poly}(\lambda/\varepsilon)}. \] The learning algorithm can be made \emph{agnostic}, given a known bound on the variance of the label marginal distribution. Some known control of label scale is information-theoretically necessary. For arbitrary labels with variance at most $V^2 \ge 1$, the complexity is \[
  (d+1)^{\mathsf{poly}(V\lambda/\varepsilon)}, \] and the error is $\mathsf{opt} + \varepsilon$, where $\mathsf{opt}$ is the minimal error among Lipschitz approximators.
  Our approach combines $L_1$ polynomial regression under a convex gradient constraint with local correction of the Lipschitz property. The learner finds a polynomial that, after smoothing and clipping its range, is very close to a canonical Lipschitz correction of itself, the lower Lipschitz envelope. Our local corrector modifies the lower envelope by replacing distances to sublevel sets with a Gaussian sampling proxy, allowing the construction to be locally and stably estimated from samples.

authors.name: Arsen Vasilyan
authors.institution: The University of Texas at Austin

papers.title: Geometrically Constrained Learning I: Agnostically Learning Adversarially Robust Classifiers
papers.abstract:
We study agnostic learning under the Gaussian distribution with guarantees on both classification error and robustness to adversarial perturbations. We say that a function has boundary profile $K \ge 1$ if, for all $r > 0$, the probability that a point lies within Euclidean distance $r$ of the classification boundary is at most $Kr$. We give an algorithm that takes a robustness radius parameter $r$ and learns a hypothesis with boundary volume $O(Kr)$ and classification error $\mathsf{opt}_K + \varepsilon$, where $\mathsf{opt}_K$ is the minimum classification error among functions with boundary profile at most $K$.
  For general $r$, $K$, and $\varepsilon$, the algorithm runs in time $d^{\widetilde{O}(K^2/\varepsilon^2 + K^4r^2/\varepsilon^4)}$. In particular, in the $Kr = O(\varepsilon)$ regime, the algorithm runs in time $d^{\widetilde{O}(K^2/\varepsilon^2)}$. Up to logarithmic factors in the exponent, this matches the statistical query lower bound for agnostically learning the $K$-profile class without recovering robustness. For natural geometric classes, including convex sets and Boolean combinations of halfspaces, this matches the corresponding surface-area-based running-time bound for non-robust agnostic learning via $L_1$ polynomial regression, up to logarithmic factors in the exponent.
  Our algorithm performs $L_1$ error minimization over polynomials, with an auxiliary coordinate roughly standing in for distance to the boundary. A convex constraint on the gradient of the polynomial, in this $(d+1)$-dimensional space, produces local certificates of the range of the polynomial on balls of radius $r$. Our algorithm finds a polynomial such that these certified ranges are small, then obtains a robust classifier via randomized rounding and partitioning of the domain.

authors.name: Arsen Vasilyan
authors.institution: The University of Texas at Austin

papers.title: COMPASS: Cross-modal Observation with Multi-Path Adaptive Stopping and Selection for Early Time Series Classification
papers.abstract: Early time-series classification (ETSC) balances predictive performance against the amount of observed data. In multimodal settings, modality-associated and fused branches may differ in predictive ability at the same observed prefix, motivating joint decisions about when to stop and which branch should provide the final prediction. We propose COMPASS, a two-stage framework that preserves two modality-associated temporal branches and one fusion branch. The first stage combines cross-modal feature exchange and gated fusion with branch-wise supervision at every prefix. The second stage optimizes a shared four-action controller to continue observation or terminate through one of the frozen branches. Experiments on six physiological and wearable datasets compare COMPASS with multimodal adaptations of five ETSC baselines. COMPASS achieves the best average ranks in accuracy-earliness harmonic mean, AUROC, and earliness within this comparison set. At identical learned stopping times, branch selection improves mean accuracy over fusion readout on five of the six datasets, with gains of 2.35 and 2.16 percentage points on ISRUC-Sleep and UCDDB, respectively. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first work on joint stopping and branch selection for multimodal early time series classification.

authors.name: Oscar Tai-Yuan Chen
authors.institution: National Yang Ming Chiao Tung University

authors.name: Vincent S. Tseng
authors.institution: National Yang Ming Chiao Tung University

papers.title: Determinantal upper bounds for ternary matrices
papers.abstract: We obtain a new, sharper upper bound for the determinant of a matrix of order $n \equiv 2 \pmod{3}$ with entries in the complex third-roots of unity. This bound is an analog of Ehlich's bound for binary matrices of order $n \equiv 3 \pmod{4}$ and it is obtained by first applying an appropriate normalization, or balancing, procedure for matrices with root-of-unity entries and then generalizing Ehlich's argument. This new bound achieves an asymptotic fraction of approximately 74% of the Hadamard bound.

papers.title: Skill-JEPA: Learning Planner-Aligned Action Spaces for World Models
papers.abstract: World models based on Joint-Embedding Predictive Architectures (JEPAs) learn from pixels to predict the outcome of actions in a latent space. To reach a goal, a planner samples many candidate action sequences, uses the model to predict where each one leads, and executes the best one. However, standard planners draw their candidates from a Gaussian, while the model has only seen the structured, state-dependent actions of its training data. Its predictions for such candidates are unreliable, and planning fails more often as goals move farther away. We propose Skill-JEPA, which learns an action space aligned with the planner. A variational autoencoder conditioned on the current state encodes short action sequences into latent skills with a standard Gaussian prior, and decodes them back into actions. The world model predicts the effect of skills rather than raw actions, and the planner searches over skills starting from that same Gaussian, so its candidates resemble the model's training data. Skill-JEPA adds a single module, trained end-to-end with the world model, and leaves the planner untouched, with no subgoals, hierarchy, or hand-designed skills. Across three JEPA world models and four benchmarks, average success on goals 80 steps away rises from 42% with raw actions to 62%; the gains grow with goal distance and hold across four planners. On AntMaze, a quadruped locomotion task, success on goals two maze cells away rises from 0.4% to 38%. This suggests that part of the difficulty of reaching distant goals lies in the action space, and can be removed without changing the planner.

papers.title: CarrierKV: An Edge LLM Accelerator with Positional Carrier Decomposition for Low-Bit KV Cache
papers.abstract: Long-context decoding on edge devices is limited by DRAM, because every generated token reads the whole, growing KV cache. 4-bit block-scaled formats such as NVFP4 reduce this traffic but degrade accuracy: on Qwen3-4B, NVFP4 lowers 32K RULER (seven tasks) from 92.6 to 79.4, and a Hadamard rotation lowers it further to 57.7. We observe that most of the key energy is a positional carrier, one per-head vector that rotary position embedding (RoPE) rotates with position. In NVFP4, it sets the shared scale of most key blocks and lowers the signal-to-quantization-noise ratio of the content by about 5 dB, nearly one bit, yet it depends only on that vector and the position. We therefore introduce positional carrier decomposition, which removes the carrier before RoPE and stores only the content residual. We design a KV path that rotates and quantizes keys only after this removal and computes each attention score directly on the 4-bit code. We also design a positional phase engine that regenerates the carrier's score term for one key per cycle. At the same cache size as NVFP4, CarrierKV raises 32K RULER on Qwen3-4B from 79.4 to 91.1 and lowers the 32K PG19 perplexity increase of NVFP4 by 1.8 to 5.9 times on four models, outperforming SageAttention and P3-LLM on all four. Its loss also stays nearly flat as the cache grows, while that of NVFP4 rises. In a 22 nm FDSOI process at 600 MHz, CarrierKV's hardware increases the area of the NVFP4 accelerator by 2.9% and the energy of a 20K-token reasoning request on Qwen3-4B by 0.12% at the same decode latency. On Qwen3-4B at 32K, CarrierKV has a better RULER score than FP8 keys (91.1 against 89.3) and uses 13.7% less energy per token. The decomposition also lowers the 32K perplexity increase of 3-bit TurboQuant keys on Qwen3-4B from 69.7 to 0.76.

papers.title: Do DeepONet Trunk-Basis Preconditioners Need Training?
papers.abstract: Trunk-basis (TB) preconditioners build the coarse space of a two-level Schwarz preconditioner from the trunk functions of a trained deep operator network (DeepONet), restricted to subdomains. Their effectiveness has been attributed to spectral bias since networks learn low frequencies first, complementing a smoother that removes the high-frequency error. Spectral bias, however, is a property of training, whereas a randomly initialized trunk with a smooth activation is already smooth. We therefore ask whether TB preconditioners need training. In one dimension, we prove that on each subdomain the span of untrained trunk functions is close to the space of low-degree polynomials under suitable nondegeneracy assumptions. Numerically, for the Poisson equation and three-dimensional linear elasticity with constant coefficients, untrained TB and piecewise polynomial coarse spaces of equal dimension yield close conjugate gradient iteration counts, while training with the standard \(\ell^2\) loss sometimes increases them. Training can improve iteration counts when high-contrast coefficients make the low-energy modes non-smooth, and if the loss measures the error in the energy norm. For the Poisson equation with contrast \(10^5\), energy-trained TB coarse spaces need fewer iterations than piecewise polynomials of equal dimension, whereas \(\ell^2\)-trained ones do not. For a topology-optimized elastic cantilever with contrast \(10^6\), the energy-trained TB space enriched with the rigid-body modes gives the fewest iterations at larger coarse dimensions. This suggests that for neural operator-based hybrid solvers, a network's inductive bias and training objective should match the solver.

papers.title: Keep the Process, Change the Supplier: Runtime Governance for Tool-Using AI Agents
papers.abstract: Tool-using AI agents propose actions whose authorization and external effects cannot be inferred from generated text alone. We study an execution boundary that separates agent proposals from business-controlled authority, context disclosure, and supplier selection. The Open Process Control Plane (OPCP) mediates capability calls and records uncertain outcomes when a supplier may have acted without returning an acceptable reply. We evaluate this runtime with scripted requests and synthetic suppliers: 2,400 fault episodes across four policies, 60 process-termination/restart episodes, 19,000 timed calls across 19 configurations, five targeted mutations over 43 fixtures, and 160 substitution records. No language model or autonomous agent is evaluated. OPCP and a conservative composition agree on all measured fault outcomes. Both recover after definite refusal without cross-supplier duplication; retry-all duplicates effects in every tested lost-reply-after-commit case. Persistent runtime state prevents cross-supplier replay in the restart experiments, while same-supplier duplicate prevention also requires supplier idempotency. At 128 suppliers, best-score routing has a median latency of 1.411 ms versus 0.261 ms for pinned routing. All five selected mutations are detected, and record enumeration exposes acceptance of an empty regression set. These results characterize an execution mechanism relevant to agent governance, including its costs and assumption boundaries. They do not establish improved agent task success, prompt-injection resistance, or real-vendor model portability.

papers.title: Kinetic Arrest of a Disordered First-Order Phase Transition in Strained V2O3 Thin Films
papers.abstract: We develop a continuum phenomenological theory for the kinetic arrest (KA) of a first-order phase transition (FOPT), taking the thermal and electric field-driven metal-insulator transition (MIT) in epitaxial V2O3 thin films as a prototype. By defining a coarse-grained mesoscopic order parameter representing the metallic volume fraction coupled to the primary structural monoclinic distortion, we formulate a Time-Dependent Ginzburg-Landau (TDGL) framework integrated with a non-local elastic interaction kernel and an Imry-Wortis quenched disorder landscape. We derive an explicit dynamic criterion for the kinetic arrest boundary TK(E) by analyzing the divergence of the intrinsic order-parameter relaxation time relative to experimental observation timescales. Our framework rigorously decouples the thermodynamic driving force from the kinetic activation barrier. We demonstrate that epitaxial substrate-induced clamping elevates local elastic barriers, pinning domain boundaries and stabilizing an arrested, inhomogeneous mosaic of metallic and insulating phases down to cryogenic temperatures. The simulated transformation kinetics exhibit an Avrami exponent suppression to values n < 1, reflecting slow, hindered domain-wall propagation. Furthermore, we examine the effect of an external electric field as an isothermal mechanism that lowers this kinetic barrier, providing a phenomenological description of threshold de-arrest and multi-level resistance states. We critically discuss this electronic barrier-lowering mechanism in comparison with electrothermal Joule heating, establish diagnostic criteria to distinguish them, and contextualize these non-equilibrium dynamics with related phenomena in disordered superconducting films.

papers.title: Explicit Style Extraction for Personalized Long-Form Text Generation
papers.abstract: Personalized long-form generation asks a language model to write new text the way a specific user would. The standard recipe, retrieval-augmented generation, places a few of the user's past texts in the prompt but leaves the model to decide what to take from them. We introduce StylePrism, a taxonomy of 28 stylistic aspects in seven categories, and SP-Refine, an inference-time method that makes style extraction an explicit step: the model first fills StylePrism with the user's patterns, quoted evidence, and habits to avoid, then drafts from the user's samples and revises the draft twice against this profile, guided by its own style scores. On the three long-form tasks of LongLaMP with three LLMs, SP-Refine outperforms LongLaMP's retrieval-augmented baseline in 25 of 27 ROUGE and METEOR comparisons, by 10.2% on average and by up to 35.8%. Annotating users' own texts with the extracted profiles shows that StylePrism captures concrete, checkable habits, from the order of rhetorical moves to a reviewer's sign-off. Ablations show that the profile helps as revision guidance, not as a replacement for the samples: writing from the profile alone is worse in all 27 comparisons, while a single implicit-inference call is a cheaper alternative that comes close. Oracle variants that let the reviser see the reference, together with reference-free controls, show that larger refinement gains require information unavailable at inference time.

papers.intro:
Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to draft text on a person’s behalf: research abstracts, product reviews, social media posts. For such text to be useful, it should be correct and fluent and also sound like its author. Personalized text generation studies this problem by conditioning a model on a user’s writing history (Salemi et al., 2024b; Zhang et al., 2024), and the LongLaMP benchmark (Kumar et al., 2024) extends it to long-form outputs, where differences in style between users are most visible.

Personalized text generation studies this problem by conditioning a model on a user’s writing history (Salemi et al., 2024b; Zhang et al., 2024), and the LongLaMP benchmark (Kumar et al., 2024) extends it to long-form outputs, where differences in style between users are most visible.

The dominant approach is retrieval-augmented personalization: retrieve the user’s past texts that are most relevant to the current input and place them in the prompt (Salemi et al., 2024b; Kumar et al., 2024; Salemi et al., 2024a). Retrieval decides which samples the model sees, but says little about what the model should take from them. In LongLaMP, the retrieved samples are followed by a single instruction such as “Following the given patterns”. Whether the model attends to sentence rhythm, hedging, discourse moves, or formatting is left implicit.

papers.title: A Frugal AI Framework for India: Responsible and Right-sized AI
papers.abstract: India's AI debate often swings between two insufficient options: replicating the compute-intensive, capital-heavy foundation-model programmes of the United States or China, or remaining a downstream adopter of foreign AI with localised interfaces and safeguards. Neither serves a country that must deliver AI to a very large, diverse population across uneven infrastructure and within constrained budgets. This white paper from the Centre for Responsible AI (CeRAI), IIT Madras, proposes a third path: Responsible Frugal AI, which applies principle-based frugal engineering alongside Responsible AI. Responsible Frugal AI is right-sized AI: it fixes the functional requirement first, asks whether AI is needed at all, and then chooses the smallest sufficient model, meeting the requirement with minimal resources while keeping a verified margin, robustness and responsible governance. The framework applies frugality across four dimensions (data, compute, model and operations) through seven levers spanning the AI lifecycle, each with practices and measures. It calls for public AI rails, vernacular-first design, measured resource use, human oversight for high-stakes decisions, and a cap on total resource consumption so that efficiency gains are not cancelled out by rising usage. We argue that India is resource-imbalanced rather than resource-poor, and that frugal principles offer the most viable route to population-scale deployment, fit naturally with India's digital public infrastructure, and make sovereignty operational by preserving India's capacity to specify, deploy, govern, inspect and adapt its AI systems. A seven-point adoption checklist and eleven policy statements translate the framework into practice, positioning AI in India as a responsible, frugal public-value system that maximises social value per rupee and per joule.

papers.title: Inverse scattering for the one-dimensional discrete Schr\"odinger operator: a computational perspective
papers.abstract: We revisit inverse scattering for the one-dimensional discrete Schr\"odinger operator with compactly supported perturbation. We consider a computational perspective, adapted to the case of a digitally sampled reflection coefficient, to determine the perturbation in the form of a Jacobi matrix, including a computation of the length of the smallest interval supporting the perturbation. A new representation of scattering data in terms of orthogonal polynomials underpins the computational results. A key technical role is played by polynomials on the circle constructed from pairs of successive orthogonal polynomials on the line. The inverse algorithm is demonstrated on numerical examples.

papers.title: Decoupling Entropic and Enthalpic Elasticity in Crosslinked Polymer Nanocomposites
papers.abstract: Nanoparticle-induced local interface regions significantly enhance the bulk mechanical behavior of polymer nanocomposites, yet their energetic contribution in crosslinked elastomer networks remains poorly understood. Here, we decouple the entropic and enthalpic contributions to the elasticity of crosslinked poly(dimethylsiloxane) nanocomposites using temperature-dependent thermomechanical measurements. While the measured bulk elastic modulus exhibits a monotonic increase with nanoparticle volume fraction $\phi_{\rm n}$, we observe that the effective crosslink density initially increases before saturating at larger $\phi_{\rm n}$. These results are independently validated across two nanoparticle systems (silica and titania) and directly confirmed by X-ray scattering experiments on silica-based composites, highlighting the generality of the observation. The trends in effective crosslink density indicate that the elastic response is predominantly entropy-driven at low nanoparticle concentrations, whereas enthalpic contributions become increasingly significant at higher loadings. Assuming a linear superposition of interface and bulk contributions, these results reveal that the effective crosslink density at the particle interface decreases by an order of magnitude below a critical mean interparticle separation, indicating that localized particle proximity and clustering constrain the entropic elasticity at higher loadings.

papers.title: Post-Quantum Migration in Brownfield 5G Core Networks: Verified Hybrid Key Establishment, Performance, and Rollback
papers.abstract: Migrating brownfield 5G Core networks to post-quantum cryptography (PQC) is difficult because deployed network functions, base images, and TLS libraries evolve under different upgrade constraints. This paper evaluates a deployment-controlled migration strategy that enables hybrid post-quantum/traditional key establishment through externally deployed Boundary Cryptographic Execution Entities (BCEEs), without modifying participating network function source code. The approach is evaluated using the Open5GS AMF-NRF Service-Based Interface as a representative 5G Core scenario. Classical and hybrid configurations are compared under an unchanged mediation topology. Packet-level analysis confirms successful negotiation of X25519MLKEM768, and functional validation demonstrates that representative SBI procedures remain operational through the mediated path. In 120 NF-registration transactions, the median AMF-facing registration latency increased from 22.968 ms under the classical state to 26.351 ms under the hybrid state, reflecting a 3.383 ms (14.73 percent) increase, with a whole-block 95 percent confidence interval of [1.193, 7.872] ms. At the mediated TLS boundary, the hybrid configuration shows a 4.599 ms higher median segment-local TLS-establishment time than the classical configuration. These two reported differences reflect system-level runtime effects and do not isolate key-encapsulation cost. Packet evidence verifies rollback from hybrid-mediated operation to classical mediated operation and, separately, restoration of the native direct path. NF-facing compatibility legs remained plaintext and outside the hybrid post-quantum scope. The results demonstrate a packet-verifiable and manually reversible brownfield mechanism for introducing hybrid post-quantum key establishment on a controlled 5G SBI segment.

papers.title: Hard X-ray spectroscopy of a short-period asynchronous polar: IGR J19552+0044
papers.abstract: IGR J19552+0044 is an asynchronous polar with a beat modulation of $\approx2$ days due to $\approx3$% spin-orbit asynchronism. We present the first hard X-ray properties of this system using a NuSTAR observation. Spectral modeling yields a shock temperature of $kT_{\rm s}=44.50^{+3.60}_{-3.29}$ keV, implying a white dwarf mass of $M_{\rm WD}\geq 0.85\,M_\odot$. We infer an average accretion rate of $\dot{M}\sim 3.0\times 10^{-11}\,M_\odot\,{\rm yr}^{-1}$, consistent with expectations for short-period systems (orbital period $<2$ h). Even at this low accretion rate, we detect a significant Compton reflection component that gives a shock height of $H\sim 0.3\,R_{\rm WD}$. Time-resolved spectroscopy of the observation, covering $\approx61$% of a beat cycle, reveals a variation in $\dot{M}$ by a factor of $\sim 4.5$, providing X-ray evidence for the magnetic valve mechanism. Despite the large variations in $\dot{M}$, no significant change in shock temperature is observed. This weak thermal response constrains the shock structure on the white dwarf surface, favoring a shock height that remains approximately constant as $\dot{M}$ changes, potentially due to variations in the fractional accretion area $f$.
