papers.title: Interaction and confinement effects for a ${}^6\mathrm{Li}_2$ condensate in a shaken lattice
papers.abstract: A shaken optical lattice can form Floquet-engineered band structures. For a one-dimensional lattice, this method can hybridize the ground and first excited bands into a double-well dispersion. A molecular Bose-Einstein condensate (mBEC) loaded into this band bifurcates into two clusters at opposite quasimomenta, but short cluster lifetimes (2 ms to 3 ms) have limited earlier work. We improve our $^6$Li mBEC experiment by aligning the lattice axis with the trap and using a multifrequency shaking sequence to counterdiabatically load into the double-well minima. Together, these improvements allow us to extend the experiment timescale beyond 10 ms. At these longer times the momentum distribution depends qualitatively on the confinement. With stronger confinement in the lattice direction, there is a peak in the momentum distribution at the Brillouin zone edge. Shaking-frequency spectroscopy confirms this zone edge population and shows it splits roughly equally between the ground and first excited bands. The longer lifetime also lets us ramp the magnetic field from 650 G, where molecules interact weakly, to 800 G, near the Feshbach resonance. As the interaction strengthens, the bifurcation weakens and disappears. We suggest that the increased molecular size causes this change.

papers.title: Data-Adaptive Entropy-Based Moment Reduction for Vlasov-Poisson-Dougherty Dynamics
papers.abstract: We develop a data-adaptive entropy-based moment method for the Vlasov-Poisson-Dougherty system with self-consistent temperature. A positive exponential representation augments the physical moments with data-adapted velocity functions. The collision guarantees are independent of basis construction: for every fixed basis satisfying the stated rank condition, the reduced collision step is uniquely solvable, positive, locally conservative and entropy-dissipative. These guarantees persist under a positive empirical cubature method (ECM), enabling structure-preserving collision hyper-reduction. We construct the basis by proper orthogonal decomposition (POD), fit it with a neural network and post-train it through the reduced dynamics. In two-stream relaxation, sustained heating and drive switching, one fixed post-trained basis with thirteen variables per cell attains space-time distribution errors below 0.25% against same-grid full-order solutions. Post-training lowers this error relative to the neural fit in all three tests and to POD in the two driven tests. With full-grid MUSCL retained, matched drive-switching timings give 1.36-2.89-fold online speedups over the full-order solver using 128-1024 velocity nodes.

authors.name: Jiahao Zhang
authors.institution: Chinese Academy of Medical Sciences & Peking Union Medical College

papers.title: FoRe: A Force-Guided Framework for Autonomous Grasp Recovery in Vision-Language-Action Models
papers.abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models have demonstrated strong performance in grasp-based manipulation, yet reliable recovery from local grasping failures remains challenging. Specifically, in pick-and-place tasks, policies may continue transport after a failed grasp instead of retrying, potentially reflecting overreliance on proprioceptive cues for stage progression and limited retry supervision. Existing recovery approaches typically rely on deployment-time guidance or demonstration augmentation. We introduce Force-guided Recovery (FoRe), a framework for autonomous recovery from local grasping failures. Using force feedback, FoRe partitions demonstrations into approach-grasp and transport-placement stages to train separate policies. To supplement limited retry supervision, FoRe then initializes a dedicated retry policy from the approach-grasp policy and refines it through local reinforcement learning (RL) from post-failure states. To avoid inappropriate stage progression, a controller combines force feedback with grasp-command status at inference to coordinate the stage policies, detect grasp failures, and invoke the retry policy. We also construct LIBERO-SUCTION, a force-augmented suction manipulation benchmark adapted from LIBERO, with complete demonstration trajectories for policy training. FoRe consistently improves task success rates for VLA-Adapter and $\pi_{0.5}$ on LIBERO-SUCTION, LIBERO, and real-world tasks. On LIBERO-SUCTION, average absolute gains are 18.4% and 6.5%, respectively. The corresponding real-world absolute gains are 25.0% and 21.7%. FoRe also remains effective with only one demonstration per task on both simulation benchmarks.

authors.name: Haoyuan Wang
authors.institution: Changchun University of Science and Technology

authors.name: Jian Huang
authors.institution: Sichuan Academy of Medical Sciences & Sichuan Provincial People's Hospital

papers.title: Random pullback attractors for evolution equations with nonlocal perturbations and fractional Brownian motion
papers.abstract: We study semilinear evolution equations with time-nonlocal perturbations of \(\mu\ge0\) and additive fractional Brownian noise with Hurst parameter \(H\in(1/2,1)\). Under the regularity assumptions and a globally Lipschitz nonlinearity, we establish global existence and uniqueness in the concept of pathwise mild solutions. We overcome the difficult in which the solution family lacks the cocycle property, by shifting the corresponding stochastic Volterra equation on a weighted space, and then the continuous random dynamical system follows. Based on a dissipativity condition, we establish the pullback random asymptotic compactness and the compact random pullback attractor \(\mathcal A_\mu\). Finally, we prove that the family of random pullback attractors \(\mathcal A_\mu\) is upper semicontinuous at \(\mu=0\) almost surely.

authors.name: Jianhua Huang
authors.institution: Sichuan Academy of Medical Sciences & Sichuan Provincial People's Hospital

papers.title: Connectivity-Constrained Linear System Realization: Feasibility and Realizable Sets
papers.abstract: In this paper, we first study the problem of finding a state-space realization of a given transfer function that adheres to a given connectivity pattern (i.e., support). While variants of this problem have been studied in distributed and structured control, existing work typically focuses on connectivity patterns relating to some networked plant. In contrast, we are interested in arbitrary connectivity patterns, which are relevant to modeling problems in sensorimotor neuroscience. We show that this problem is equivalent to solving a system of multivariate polynomial equations, and can be solved exactly without relaxation or approximation. We then study the reverse problem: given a connectivity pattern, what transfer functions have a state-space realization that adheres to this pattern? In other words, what transfer functions can this pattern realize? A surprising finding is that any given pattern can realize nearly all transfer functions, or very few transfer functions. We provide rigorous results and algorithms for both problems, leveraging technical machinery from algebraic geometry. The efficacy of our approach is demonstrated in examples at the end of the paper.

papers.title: SceneRuler: Measuring Physical Quantities in Video via Minimal Sufficient Reconstruction
papers.abstract: Many questions about videos ask for a number, such as how tall a person is, how far a cart travels, or how fast a ball leaves a ramp. We study this task, quantitative physical reasoning from video, where the inputs are a video, a question, and a prior of known facts such as object sizes, speeds, and distances from the camera to named objects. End-to-end video-language models lack an explicit metric scale and physical consistency, and their errors cannot be inspected. We present SceneRuler, which instead recovers a measurable physical scene and answers with that scene as evidence. Its central principle, Minimal Sufficient Reconstruction, builds, for each question, only the smallest scene that suffices to measure the asked quantity, and tests sufficiency on measurements rather than assuming it. The scene is written as a program whose structure a vision-language model writes and whose magnitudes are left to measurement. Physics-guided Fitting measures them through physical motion laws, so that gravity itself can anchor the metric scale, and marks every parameter, and the read-out of the asked quantity, as determined or undetermined. Each question receives a read-out and an answer. The read-out is the asked quantity evaluated on the scene, and it is empty when the scene does not fix that quantity. The answer is always given by a model that takes the scene as evidence. We evaluate on QuantiPhy and also apply the method to 27 in-the-wild videos that we collected, which have no ground-truth answers. On its validation split, the final answer reaches a mean relative accuracy of 0.709 against 0.624 for the strongest baseline, and the reconstruction determines the asked quantity on 47 of 158 questions, where the final answer reaches 0.781. Because every intermediate quantity is explicit, each answer can be traced to the objects, scale, and motion behind it.

authors.name: Yin Yang
authors.institution: State Key Laboratory of Coal Combustion

papers.title: A conservative latent neural ODE for stiff collisional-radiative plasma kinetics
papers.abstract: Collisional-radiative (CR) models govern the non equilibrium population kinetics of partially ionized plasmas and are a dominant cost in integrated edge and divertor plasma simulations, where a stiff system of dozens to thousands of coupled rate equations must be solved at every spatial cell and time step. We present a two-stage machine learning (ML) surrogate that replaces the direct CR solve with a compact, continuous-time, deployable dynamical model. Stage~1 is a grey-box autoencoder that compresses a high-dimensional ion population vector into a low-dimensional latent space in which four coordinates, one per charge state of the lithium system studied here, are \emph{fixed} to the physical charge-state distribution and the rest are learned. Stage~2 is a latent neural ODE that learns the continuous-time evolution of the latent variables. We (i) integrate in a density-folded, logarithmic clock on which the latent trajectory is smooth enough for an explicit integrator, (ii) sample time adaptively by latent arc length so the sharp ionization transition is resolved, (iii) add a linear damping toward an estimate of the CR steady state as a design choice, and (iv) enforce mass conservation directly. The surrogate is accurate, with a charge-state error that is unchanged under refinement of its output grid, over full-trajectory rollouts within the trained horizon, and exactly conservative: on $1480$ held-out trajectories at the trained conditions it reproduces the charge-state evolution with a median absolute error of $4.2\times10^{-3}$ on fractions in $[0,1]$, conserves mass to $10^{-7}$, {and evaluates a full sixteen-decade trajectory in ${\sim}76\,\mu$s per trajectory in batched inference on a single GPU.} A model retrained with whole $(\nA,\Te)$ grid points withheld is equally accurate at those unseen conditions.

authors.name: Xuping Xie
authors.institution: The University of Texas Medical Branch at Galveston

papers.title: Mind the Delta: Early Pruning of RTL Variants for Agentic Hardware Optimization
papers.abstract: Autonomous coding agents powered by large language models (LLMs) now write diverse microarchitectural variants of existing register-transfer level (RTL) designs at high throughput, shifting the primary bottleneck of agentic RTL optimization onto logic synthesis. Commercial toolchains take hours per variant, creating an acute compute asymmetry between proposing and evaluating variants. Existing fast evaluators falter in this regime. Subtle RTL edits trigger nonlinear synthesis shifts that learned predictors and coding agents cannot resolve, while synthesis proxies at reduced effort either alter the optimization trajectory or retain most of its runtime. Selecting a variant, however, does not require regressing absolute quality of results across designs, only identifying when a candidate cannot surpass the best completed feasible implementation. Based on the observation that synthesis trajectories share strong design-specific bias with their base design, we propose DiffScope, a training-free anytime selection framework that races full synthesis runs in parallel. By pairing live area telemetry with the already synthesized base trajectory, DiffScope cancels early mapping inflation, reducing residual variance during initial mapping by 73.6X, and stops uncompetitive runs via a lower bound calibrated on other design lineages. Across 43 design families from small blocks to processors with millions of cells, DiffScope uniquely recovers the optimum of exhaustive synthesis in every family, cuts total evaluation work by 44.9% (1.81X), and reaches 2.18X on L-tier designs.

authors.name: Kun Wang
authors.institution: University of Electronic Science and Technology of China

authors.name: Ke Xu
authors.institution: Beijing National Research Center for Information Science and Technology

papers.title: Global Strong Solutions and Large-Time Behavior for Radial Compressible Navier-Stokes Flow with Density-Dependent Viscosities on a Disk and in the Plane
papers.abstract: The two-dimensional barotropic compressible Navier-Stokes equations admit a unique global strong solution for arbitrarily large radial initial data without swirl, both on a disk with a no-slip wall and in the whole plane. On the disk we require the initial acceleration to have zero trace at the wall. The initial density is bounded away from zero and, in the plane, approaches a positive constant at infinity. The shear and second viscosities have a common density exponent between one half and one, inclusive. Throughout the strictly dissipative range of viscosity coefficients, every pressure exponent greater than or equal to one is admissible. In particular, the result applies to Marche's viscous shallow water equations on a flat bottom in the absence of rotation, bottom friction, and capillarity. These equations retain the positive second viscosity derived from free-surface flow and thus fall outside the Bresch-Desjardins relation. The density stays bounded above and away from zero uniformly in time. On the disk, the density converges exponentially to its spatial mean and the velocity to zero in the Sobolev norm of order three. In the plane, convergence in the same norm holds to the prescribed far-field state. The argument also applies to a class of non-power viscosity laws.

authors.name: Kexin Li
authors.institution: University of Electronic Science and Technology of China

papers.title: Distillation with Errors: Sparse Unbiased Backpropagation for Knowledge Distillation
papers.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) trains a student to match a teacher's output distribution. However, full-vocabulary KD requires costly output-head backpropagation. To reduce this cost, we introduce Distillation with Errors (DWE). Our key insight is that minibatch training already approximates the training gradient, so per-position backpropagation does not need to be exact. DWE therefore exploits the zero-sum structure of logit gradients to construct sparse paired gradient estimates whose expectation matches the full-vocabulary gradient. It then uses geometry-aware pairing and stratified sampling to further reduce estimation variance. We prove that the estimator is unbiased and evaluate DWE's gradient estimation accuracy and training efficiency. At the same sampling budget, DWE reduces hidden-state and output-weight gradient MSE by 63.5% and 57.9%, respectively, compared with importance sampling. In off-policy KD, it achieves up to a $1.95\times$ output-head speedup and reduces training time by 10.4-15.7% relative to full-vocabulary KD. In on-policy distillation (OPD), it achieves up to a $2.20\times$ output-head speedup. DWE maintains competitive downstream performance in both settings. Our code is available at https://github.com/dwe-lab/DWE.

authors.name: Yuxin Li
authors.institution: University of Electronic Science and Technology of China

papers.title: Crafting the Difference, Grounding the Evidence: Discriminative Concept Learning for Zero-Shot Skeleton Action Recognition
papers.abstract: LLM-generated descriptions enrich zero-shot skeleton-based action recognition but repeat cues shared by confusable actions. Their contextual semantics also lack explicit links to skeleton features. To address these challenges, we propose CRAFT, which couples Concept Refinement and Feature-grounded Tokens. Hard-negative-conditioned generation and contrastive scoring identify concepts that distinguish each action from its closest rivals. Unique-QDPP selects complementary descriptions within each semantic slot and prevents their reuse across slots. This bank supervises learnable concept tokens that read motion and context cues from each skeleton. On fixed NTU-60 and NTU-120 splits, CRAFT improves five baselines spanning four recognition paradigms. ZSL accuracy and GZSL harmonic mean increase on every baseline-split pair, by 5.4 and 5.9 percentage points on average. Random-split experiments extend these gains to three datasets, including PKU-MMD. Code will be released after acceptance.

papers.title: Balanced Divide and Conquer for Rooted Maximum Agreement Forests
papers.abstract: We develop a balanced divide-and-conquer framework for the maximum agreement forest problem on rooted binary phylogenetic tree--forest instances. The goal is a common subforest with the fewest components; budget $k$ bounds the increase relative to the input forest. We balance edges associated with an unknown optimum to obtain three subproblems with smaller budgets. Branching separates the inputs, while temporary marker leaves allow a global optimum to be recovered from independently computed optimal solutions. For any fixed $B>\varphi=(1+\sqrt5)/2$, the framework converts a tree--forest solver running in $O^*(B^k)$ time into one running in $O^*((\sqrt{\varphi B})^k)$ time. Starting from an $O^*(2.3391^k)$-time solver, two applications yield an $O^*(1.7743^{k^*})$-time fixed-parameter algorithm for two trees, where $k^*$ is the number of components in a maximum agreement forest minus one. For every fixed $\varepsilon>0$, a fixed number of applications yields $O^*((\varphi+\varepsilon)^{k^*})$ time. Here $O^*$ suppresses polynomial factors, whose degree and constants may depend on $\varepsilon$.

papers.title: Real-Anchored Complementary Evidence for Generalizable AI-Generated Image Detection
papers.abstract: Evolving generative models challenge detector generalization, as methods trained on generated examples may rely on generator-specific cues. By contrast, authentic photographs share regularities rooted in physical image formation and acquisition, providing a common reference beyond individual generators. Building on these regularities, we propose Real-Anchored Complementary Evidence (RACE), which learns complementary global and local detection evidence using only authentic training images. First, the global pathway combines frozen and learned representations to assess proximity to authentic references. Next, it incorporates responses to controlled perturbations, complementing static compatibility with representation sensitivity. The local pathway then reconstructs complete trace descriptors, using intermediate features and signed perturbation responses as context while restricting detection evidence to static terminal-residual reconstruction errors. Finally, authentic-image statistics align the global and local scores for fusion, and an independent authentic set calibrates a decision threshold held fixed across test generators. Across six benchmarks, RACE achieves the highest average AUROC of 96.59% among the compared methods, reaching 97.18% on five out-of-domain benchmarks. Together with robustness to image perturbations and variation in authentic-image sources, these results support authentic-image regularities as a transferable basis for detection across diverse generators and image conditions.

authors.name: Zhenyu Shao
authors.institution: University of Chinese Academy of Sciences

papers.title: Mem-X: A Memory-Dependent Cross-Episode Benchmark for Vision-and-Language Navigation
papers.abstract: Long-term memory enables embodied agents to reuse past observations across tasks. However, existing cross-episode vision-and-language navigation (VLN) benchmarks often leave it unclear whether successful navigation relies on historical memory or current exploration. We introduce Mem-X, a benchmark designed to evaluate memory-dependent cross-episode VLN. Mem-X organizes episodes into sessions in which subsequent instructions refer to objects or routes encountered in earlier episodes. Its three levels evaluate historical-object recall, in-memory localization and episodic indexing, and off-memory relocalization and historical-route reproduction. For the latter two levels, agents receive episode-local poses but no transformations between episode frames, requiring them to establish spatial correspondence with historical memory. Mem-X comprises 2,071 episodes across 710 sessions in 34 scenes, including 1,204 memory-dependent episodes. We also provide MemBridge, a modular baseline that combines semantic scene memory, cross-episode localization, and coarse-to-fine retrieval to support existing VLN agents. Experiments with state-of-the-art VLN methods demonstrate the benefits of MemBridge while revealing substantial room for improvement on memory-dependent navigation. The benchmark and baseline code are available at https://github.com/NJU-R-L-Group-Embodied-Lab/Mem-X.

authors.name: Junhui Guo
authors.institution: State Key Laboratory of Advanced Separation Membrane Materials

authors.name: You Wu
authors.institution: Kunming University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Lift Out, Kick In: Decoupling Event Effects for Time Series Forecasting
papers.abstract: Real-world time series are often shaped by exogenous events whose effects are superimposed on the system's underlying temporal dynamics. Historical observations therefore entangle persistent dynamics with event-induced deviations, making it difficult to determine which patterns should be extrapolated and which should be attributed to specific event contexts. Existing event-aware forecasting methods can incorporate event information or model event-related variation, but typically treat historical event attribution and future event generation separately. We propose Loki (Lift Out, Kick In), a general event-aware forecasting framework built on a shared Event Response Function (ERF). The ERF models event effects according to event type and relative temporal position and is shared across the historical and forecast windows. Loki lifts out estimated event-induced deviations from historical observations before forecasting, then uses the same ERF to kick in responses to known future events. This formulation separates event-response modeling from temporal forecasting while coupling historical attribution and future generation through a shared mechanism. Across five forecasting benchmarks, Loki achieves the best standardized MAE on all five datasets, reducing error by approximately 2.2%-11.7% over the strongest non-Loki baseline. Ablations and controlled analyses further support the roles of Lift Out, Kick In, shared response modeling, and compatibility across forecasting backbones.

authors.name: Xiaocen Guo
authors.institution: University of Electronic Science and Technology of China

papers.title: Linear Convergence of Adaptive Accelerated Gradient Methods: A Unified Framework
papers.abstract: We establish a unified Lyapunov framework for adaptive accelerated gradient methods on smooth, strongly convex objectives. Conditions on local curvature, stepsize ratios, and coefficient variation ensure eventual linear convergence without assuming stepsize convergence. We verify these conditions for specified AdaNAG-G, smooth unconstrained AC-FGM, and AdaAGM policies and use them to design VC-FG and CC-FG. The verified adaptive main iterations require neither global smoothness nor strong-convexity parameters and avoid restart and backtracking. The framework also sharpens a fixed-step FISTA/NAG-type bound. Experiments on four smooth, strongly convex problem families illustrate complementary performance of the new methods.

papers.title: Large deviations and conditional laws for a time-integrated logarithm of averaged Gaussian squares
papers.abstract: Systems with identical instantaneous power distributions can have very different probabilities of insufficient service over a fixed interval. We study the lower tail of the time-integrated logarithm of a weighted mean of $d$ independent squared Gaussian paths as $d\to\infty$. A global entropy inequality resolves the nonconvex service constraint, identifies the unique Gaussian minimizer and controls the nonlinear likelihood weight far from that minimizer. Combined with a joint local limit, it yields sharp probabilities at fixed internal thresholds and conditional path laws: a Fredholm determinant enters the leading factor, and tangential Gaussian fluctuations are independent of the exponential service deficit. The approximations extend through moderate deviations to the central scale. For stationary Ornstein--Uhlenbeck paths, cancellation in the radial likelihood expansion yields relative error $O(d^{-1})$ on compact positive parameter families with proportions and saddles separated from zero. Genuine temporal covariance attenuation by correlation kernels for a type of positive limiting proportion increases the lower-tail rate, yet the finite-sample outage distributions cross near typical service. Thus one-time power distributions alone do not determine reliability.

authors.name: Haoran Xu
authors.institution: University of Electronic Science and Technology of China

papers.title: Coding Length and Optimal Power Allocation in Correlated Block Fading
papers.abstract: A codeword spans a fixed number of correlated Gaussian fading blocks. The receiver knows the gains and the transmitter knows only their law. At fixed average signal-to-noise ratio, we require the decoding error probability to decay exponentially with the number of receive antennas. When does outage predict the achievable rate? If block length grows faster than the number of antennas, outage gives the limiting optimal rate. If both grow to infinity at a fixed positive ratio of block length to array size, outage strictly overestimates the limiting rate. We determine the critical ratio above which positive rates are possible. For sufficiently large finite ratios, we find the exact limiting rate over all codes satisfying a total energy constraint on each codeword. The leading rate loss is inversely proportional to the ratio. Its coefficient depends on Gaussian channel dispersion at the most likely fade causing outage and on how quickly the outage rate decreases as the required error exponent increases. In the long-block limit, equal power loses rate on every window of three or more blocks under stationary first-order autoregressive fading with positive lag-one correlation. In a different three-block channel with identical marginal gains, tightening the reliability requirement first makes it optimal to leave the middle block unused and later to use it again.

authors.name: Haoran Xu
authors.institution: University of Electronic Science and Technology of China

papers.title: No roughening transition for the Ising model on $\mathbb{Z}^d$ with $d \geq 4$
papers.abstract: Consider the Ising measure $\mu_{\Lambda_n,\beta}^{\text{Dob}}$ on $\Lambda_n:=([-n,n]^{d-1}\times[-n,n-1]) \cap \mathbb{Z}^d$ at inverse temperature $\beta$ with all plus boundary condition at heights $z \geq 0$ and all minus boundary condition at heights $z<0$. Let $\beta_c(d)$ be the critical inverse temperature. For every $d \geq 4$ and $\beta>\beta_c(d)$, we prove that $\mu_{\Lambda_n,\beta}^{\text{Dob}}(\sigma_0)$ has a positive lower bound independent of $n$. As a consequence, any Dobrushin state (i.e., a subsequential limit of $\mu_{\Lambda_n,\beta}^{\text{Dob}}$) is not translation invariant for those $(d,\beta)$, and thus there is no roughening transition when $d \geq 4$.

papers.title: The Construction of Directed Partial Orders on the Complex Field by Puiseux Series and Stratification
papers.abstract: Birkhoff and Pierce asked in 1956 whether the complex field C admits a lattice order compatible with the ring operations. Schwartz and Yang proved in 2011 that C admits directed partial orders. We give a new construction that by using a transcendence basis of C over Q, we embed C into a field of Puiseux series F{{s}}, so that every complex number acquires a series expansion, and we define positivity by a condition on the leading coefficient. Every directed partial order we construct is placed in a stratification by how much of the expansion a rule has to read. Reading one term, a window of fixed width, or a sensitivity condition on small changes, we obtain five nested conditions and six types. Relative to the fixed level valuation, cones satisfying B correspond to the cards satisfying a product and a sum condition. Cones satisfying C are never lattice orders, which excludes Types 1, 2, 3. We give an example of Type 4 that is not a lattice order either. The existence of a lattice order on C and the existence of orders of Types 5 and 6 still remain open. This is a stratification rather than a complete classification because only Types 1 - 4 are shown to be nonempty.

papers.title: Eigenvalues and Resonances of the Kramers-Fokker-Planck Operator in the Large-Friction Limit
papers.abstract: We study the eigenvalues and resonances of the Kramers-Fokker-Planck operator by the methods of analytic dilation and phase-space deformation. We prove that in the large-friction limit $\gamma\to+\infty$, there are neither eigenvalues nor resonances away from the thresholds $\gamma N$, and that near each threshold $\gamma k$, there exists a bijection between the eigenvalues and resonances of the Kramers-Fokker-Planck operator and those of the Witten Laplacian at the level $k$, $-\Delta_V^{(k)}=-\Delta_V\otimes 1_{\mu_k}-d\Gamma_k(\operatorname{Hess}V)$. We also show that each negative eigenvalue of $-\Delta_V^{(k)}$, $k\geq 1$, produces a pole of the resolvent at distance of order $\gamma^{-1}$ below $\gamma k$, whose imaginary part is $O(e^{-c\gamma})$ for every $c<2\delta_V$. Here $\delta_V$ is the width of a strip of analyticity of $V$.

papers.title: GAAFormer: Geometry-Anchored Attention Transformer for Joint Point Cloud Denoising and Upsampling
papers.abstract: Point cloud denoising and upsampling require samples that accurately recover the underlying surface from noisy or sparse observations. A central challenge in both tasks is preserving surface coverage while refining point locations. We introduce GAAFormer (Geometry-Anchored Attention Transformer), a unified generative octree transformer that performs both tasks with a shared network. Its decoder anchors attention neighborhoods to geometry, providing spatial context for occupancy prediction and point generation. Fixed voxel windows and alternating shifts preserve the grouping of surviving nodes as the output tree changes. The design retains the encoder, positional encoding, prediction heads, and parameter count of a serialized-attention backbone. We establish a deletion-consistency property of the neighborhood rule and evaluate both tasks using the same model. On PUNet, GAAFormer achieves a mean Chamfer distance (CD) of $6.0643\times10^{-5}$, reducing CD and Hausdorff distance by 3.35% and 19.34%, respectively, relative to the serialized backbone. For upsampling, it achieves CD values of $0.8475$, $1.7057$, and $1.0147$ ($\times10^{-5}$) on PU-GAN, PU1K, and Sketchfab, respectively, with improvements in CD, Hausdorff distance, and point-to-surface distance over the same backbone on PU-GAN and Sketchfab. These results establish a single architecture for point cloud denoising and upsampling. Within the shared encoder-decoder, the same geometry-anchored attention module improves both noise removal and dense point generation without task-specific redesign or additional parameters.

Point cloud denoising removes geometric noise, while point cloud upsampling generates dense samples from sparse observations. Both tasks require accurate recovery of the underlying surface: predicted points must lie near the surface and cover its geometry. A unified network must therefore suppress noise and generate new samples while preserving geometric detail and surface coverage. Figure 1 contrasts task-specific pipelines with our unified architecture, in which the same geometric attention module and network weights support both tasks.

Transformer backbones add feature interactions over groups of octree nodes. Serialized neighborhoods make these interactions efficient [17, 19], but their membership depends on positions in a compact node sequence. In a generative decoder, this sequence is rebuilt as predicted occupancy changes.

An incorrect coarse occupancy decision removes all descendant samples, so finer coordinate refinement cannot restore the excluded region. This creates a shared difficulty: denoising must suppress perturbations while retaining valid surface regions, whereas upsampling must extend geometric evidence into sparsely sampled regions. Both tasks therefore require spatially consistent attention neighborhoods throughout tree generation.

papers.title: How Many Bytes Has a BPE Model Seen? Estimating Byte-Token Exposure in Pretraining from Corpus Statistics and Embedding Norms
papers.abstract: Byte-level BPE vocabularies retain 256 single-byte fallback tokens. When converting such a model into a pure byte-level model, these tokens provide the starting embeddings. How much training have they received? We estimate byte-token exposure in Qwen3.8 using two independent routes. First, we tokenize 540 MB of public corpora covering 40 domains and 33 languages, then combine per-domain token shares with assumed pretraining mixtures. Single-byte tokens account for 13 to 36% of tokens, mostly ASCII; genuine UTF-8 fallback bytes (0x80-0xFF) account for 0.15 to 0.27% under mainstream mixtures, or about 2 billion occurrences per trillion pretraining tokens. Fallback rates vary by four orders of magnitude across languages, reflecting how well each script is covered by the vocabulary. Second, we analyze embedding and output-matrix row norms for four open models, using untrained padding rows as a zero-exposure baseline and ordinary tokens with known frequencies for calibration. In all four models, the 13 bytes that cannot occur in valid UTF-8 remain at initialization, while every legal high byte lies in a high-frequency band. For Qwen3.8, the norm-based estimate agrees with the corpus estimate within a factor of four. The norm-frequency relation eventually folds, so inversion is useful only as a model-specific, order-of-magnitude estimate. No private data were used.

papers.title: Do Alice and Bob Dream of the Oracle? Wishful Cryptanalysis
papers.abstract: For two millennia, offense and defense have forged cryptographic security boundaries. Tools automated calculation and search, while humans drove discovery. Foundation models now mark a shift from automated computation to intelligent scientific discovery. Because cryptanalysis rests on exact mathematical definitions and immediately executable truth, it offers a proving ground for autonomous intelligence to move past security reliant on scarce human attention and explore structures beyond human working memory. Unguided models stall between two opposite traps: authority hallucination, where they surrender whenever prior literature declares a route blocked, and reasoning hallucination, where they produce subtle, unverifiable flaws. Closed platforms and generic agent loops further impede sustained open inquiry. We introduce wishful cryptanalysis, a harness-agnostic methodology that pairs constructive optimism against entrenched assumptions with blinded, zero-import verification against error. Agents first compress reduced-scale theory within provisioned compute so live witnesses certify their mathematics automatically. They then co-adapt primitive, algorithm, and hardware, and climb parameter ladders toward high-round theory. Applied across frontier open-weight and proprietary models with minimal human intervention beyond targets and compute, this paradigm yielded novel attack techniques and thirteen verifiable practical results across Keccak (SHA-3) and AES. These include breaking a fifteen-year-open public challenge and closing longstanding practical gaps, released alongside an early-preview open-source workbench (agent-framework). Extending Kerckhoffs's principle into the AI era, we envision an Open Oracle, an open and auditable public infrastructure that frees cryptographers to legislate security goals, challenge assumptions, distill theory, and co-design resilient standards.

authors.name: Keting Jia
authors.institution: Beijing National Research Center for Information Science and Technology

authors.name: Hongbo Yu
authors.institution: Huazhong University of Science and Technology

authors.name: Anyu Wang
authors.institution: Henan University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Decomposing images in a PRISM: A Single-Source Multi-View Framework for Image Representation
papers.abstract: Multi-view learning has shown that combining complementary views can improve predictive performance, yet many datasets provide a single raw source of information. How can multiple useful views be constructed from one source? We propose PRISM (Plural Representations of Images via Structural Maps), a framework that transforms an image into representations with distinct inductive biases through explicit structural maps, together with a protocol for measuring what each view contributes. We evaluate PRISM-HD, a hand-designed instantiation of PRISM in which the constructed views are summarized through representation-specific descriptors, on three artistic and four non-artistic image datasets. Analyses at a fixed feature budget show that the gains of the structural views are not explained by feature dimensionality alone. PRISM-HD by itself outperforms WND-CHARM on all seven datasets. Moreover, PRISM-HD and Fisher Vector provide complementary predictive signals: their equal-weight combination improves over the better individual representation by 5--8 percentage points on the artistic datasets. When combined with fine-tuned deep networks through a fixed parameter-free fusion rule, the PRISM-based representation improves performance on four of seven datasets and leaves it statistically unchanged on the remaining three, indicating that the constructed views provide predictive signals that are complementary to learned deep representations.

papers.title: Moments, Equilibrium Equations and Barycentric Coordinates
papers.abstract: In a previous article, we applied the classical theory of moments to establish equilibrium equations for rather general finite systems of interacting particles. An equilibrium of such a system occurs if and only if the corresponding ``zeroth'' moment $\mu_0$ and the first moment $\mu_1$ vanish. Our focus then was on the relationship between $\mu_0$, $\mu_1$ and the second moment $\mu_2$ in order to produce systems of equilibrium equations solely dependent on mutual distances, including a generalization of the Albouy-Chenciner equations for central configurations in Celestial Mechanics. In the present work, we explore in depth the condition of simultaneously vanishing $\mu_0$ and $\mu_1$ on its own. This condition defines at once a vector space which is studied via barycentric coordinates and elementary exterior algebra, thereby yielding families of equilibrium equations for systems with any consistent number $n$ of particles and dimension $d$. As before, the present equilibrium equations are homogeneous as well as invariant by oriented isometries (for interactions depending only on mutual distances). Our method also develops and extends the approach by A. Albouy from central configurations of codimension $c=(n-1)-d$ equal to one, the so-called Dziobek configurations, to equilibria of systems of interacting particles of arbitrary codimension. Despite the similar appearance, our generalized Albouy equations constitute new equilibrium equations when $c$ is greater than one, even in the case of central configurations. The paper closes with applications to central configurations, with specific results for $n=5,6$ in dimension $d=2$.

papers.title: Tuning the Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction in CoFeB thin film heterostructures
papers.abstract: The Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya Interaction (DMI) is essential for stabilizing chiral spin textures in spintronics, yet achieving consistent quantitative measurements across different techniques remains a significant challenge. Heterostructures consisting of magnetic thin films sandwiched between non-magnetic heavy metals have been shown to possess substantial DMI; however, these vary in both magnitude and handedness for supposedly identical samples, indicating the sensitivity of DMI to both interfacial properties and measurement techniques. Here, systematic tuning of the DMI in ultra-thin magnetic heterostructures of Pt/CoFeB/Ta/Pt is achieved by varying the thickness of a tantalum sub-monolayer with thicknesses ranging from $0.1\,\mathrm{nm}$ to $0.4\,\mathrm{nm}$. The magnitude and sign of the DMI are measured using three independent methods: the parallel stripe domain model, edge nucleation field analysis, and Brillouin light scattering. The three independent approaches reveal excellent agreement within the experimental error. This ability to controllably tune and reliably quantify DMI provides a viable route toward engineering chiral magnetic textures, including domain walls and skyrmions, for next-generation spintronic devices. The necessity for precise measurements of magnetic parameters and careful attention to detail are discussed because calculations of the DMI for each technique depend on different parameters.

papers.title: Simple Routes to Turing-Like Patterns
papers.abstract: Spots, stripes, and networks recur in systems with very different microscopic dynamics, suggesting that the competing processes behind Turing-like patterns may be easy to realise. We ask whether local amplification coupled to suppression over a wider region can generate these geometries in simple systems beyond chemical reaction--diffusion models. We test this idea in two settings, a binary cellular automaton obtained by adding a distant neighbour count to Conway's Game of Life and a self-gravitating toy universe described by particle motion and two continuous fields. The automaton produces spots, stripes, and coexistence across its control plane, while a rule retaining only the two opposing counts produces islands, stripes, and holes. Directional correlations and intrinsic dimension identify the same region of orientational order. In the gravitational system, convergence increases local density while mass transport depletes the surroundings. The two-field and particle densities have a smoothed spatial correlation of $0.962$ at scale factor $a=1$ under the original force law, and strengthening its long-wavelength component drives both descriptions toward fewer dense condensations. Together, these results show how simple counting rules and redistribution of a conserved quantity can realise competing growth and suppression, providing two concrete routes by which Turing-like geometries can recur across different dynamics.

authors.name: Xiang-Ning Li
authors.institution: Ministry of Education of the People's Republic of China

papers.title: TSIR: Ray-Traced Triangle Splats for Inverse Rendering
papers.abstract: Inverse rendering enables realistic relighting for visual effects and augmented reality. However, overlapping Gaussian primitives complicate surface recovery and require costly multi-layer traversal and compositing for light transport. We propose TSIR, a two-stage inverse rendering method that reconstructs relightable triangle splats from multi-view images. The first stage prepares opaque triangle splats with learnable vertex shading normals. The second stage directly traces these surfaces to estimate materials through Monte Carlo integration of direct illumination and indirect reflections, reducing reliance on multi-layer compositing. Anti-aliasing improves rendering quality while maintaining efficiency. Experiments demonstrate higher relighting quality than the evaluated baselines and more efficient anti-aliasing than supersampling.

authors.name: Chentao Shen
authors.institution: State Key Laboratory Fluid Power and Mechatronic Systems

papers.title: CTRL: Concurrent Training and Rollout for LLM Reinforcement Learning via GPU Co-Residency
papers.abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) post-training of large language models runs two GPU workloads with different hardware demands: rollout decoding, which is dominated by memory access and whose batch shrinks as responses finish, and a dense learner. Current systems either time-share every GPU between them, paying serial phases and switches, or split GPUs into pools whose sizes change only in whole devices. We present CTRL, which makes co-residency a third RL execution layout: every GPU runs a learner rank beside a persistent rollout engine, sharing the device under CUDA MPS. A host-owned learner makes the layout fit: optimizer state stays in host memory, and policy weights stream layer by layer through a bounded GPU window. A publication gate trains each ready batch first and waits only before releasing the next policy, keeping a dropless staleness bound. A step-time bound guides compute-share selection, and a GPU-time ledger explains overlap and sharing costs. On H100, A800, and RTX 4090 GPUs with Qwen3 models, CTRL achieves 1.11-2.24$\times$ the throughput of the stronger of verl's asynchronous baselines across 24 workload settings with the staleness limit set to two, and 1.23$\times$ verl's colocate_async on eight H100 GPUs. With the same learner, co-residency is 1.10-1.26$\times$ faster than time-sharing on all three platforms and 1.10-1.30$\times$ faster than the best measured whole-GPU split on H100 DAPO-Math workloads at 256-528 trajectories per step, on four and eight GPUs.

authors.name: Zeyi Wen
authors.institution: The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology (Guangzhou)

papers.title: Isomorphic nonembeddings of Lorentz spaces under tensor products
papers.abstract:
The Lorentz quasi-norm on $L_{p,q}(0,1)$ is
  \[
  \|f\|_{p,q}
  =\left(\int_0^1 [t^{1/p}f^*(t)]^q\,\frac{dt}{t}\right)^{1/q},
  \]
where $f^*$ is the decreasing rearrangement of $|f|$. Motivated by the isomorphic classification of Lorentz spaces (KuryakovSukochev2015,HuangSukochev2021), we ask whether $\ell_{p,q}\not\hookrightarrow L_{p,q}(0,1)$ persists under projective tensoring with a common factor. For $1<p<\infty$, $1\le q<\infty$, and $p\ne q$, we obtain the following results.

Nonzero finite-dimensional factors preserve the nonembedding, as do nonzero $\ell_1$-FDD factors when $q>1$.
A single factor $U$ makes both tensor products isomorphic to $U$ throughout this range. For each pair with $q>1$, there are two
nonisomorphic separable absorbers with the metric approximation
property.
For $1<q<p<2$, a scalar $L_1(\Omega,\mu)$ factor over a standard
probability space yields an embedding exactly when the nonatomic part of $\mu$ has positive measure.

For $1\le p<\infty$ and $0<q<1$, we construct common absorbers under $r$-projective tensoring after equivalent renorming.

papers.title: The distortion problem and orthogonality
papers.abstract: Schlumprecht [Israel J. Math. 76 (1991), 81--95] constructed an arbitrarily distortable Banach space. We further study distortion on this space under orthogonality constraints and obtain the following results. The exact distortion of his renormings is preserved in every infinite-dimensional subspace when the unit vectors satisfy both mutual Birkhoff--James and isosceles orthogonality for any finite family of equivalent norms. There are basic sequences of unit vectors satisfying both orthogonality conditions pairwise whose norms in the renormed space converge to the lower distortion endpoint. The proof combines finite-dimensional norm estimates with supporting functionals and the Borsuk--Ulam theorem. Further results concern finite and approximate Roberts conditions and an obstruction to simultaneous Pythagorean orthogonality for auxiliary norms.

papers.title: Quantum-Chaos-Assisted Measure Synchronization in a Double-Well Ultracold Bose Gas
papers.abstract: This paper investigates measure synchronization (MS) in a two-component ultracold atomic system confined in a double-well potential, which realizes a quantum many-body bosonic Josephson junction. Through spectral-statistics analysis, we identify the quantum chaotic parameter regime and confirm that the system achieves MS within this regime with weak dependence on the initial energy imbalance. We further show that chaotic dynamics not only significantly shortens the time scale for establishing synchronization but is also accompanied by entanglement entropy approaching the random-state prediction. These results reveal close connections among quantum chaos, MS, and quantum entanglement in conservative quantum many-body systems and may motivate further studies on the underlying mechanisms of chaos-assisted synchronization.

authors.name: Weiping Zhang
authors.institution: Xi'an University of Architecture and Technology

papers.title: AELF: Active Terrain-Aware UAV Exploration Using a Lightweight Framework
papers.abstract: This paper presents an efficient and robust approach for autonomous aerial exploration in complex environments. Instead of relying on conventional 3D voxel-based maps for exploration, we utilize a lightweight 2.5D map framework that reduces computational overhead while preserving essential topographic information. More importantly, this representation systematically eliminates the blind voxel problem commonly encountered in voxel-based exploration due to occlusions and limited visibility. Unlike previous methods that rely on a fixed altitude scale for exploration, our approach requires no prior height information and actively adapts to terrain elevation changes during exploration. To further enhance exploration efficiency while preserving the generality of 3D exploration, we perform 2D path planning on the 2.5D map framework, which is then lifted to 3D to evaluate the cost between viewpoints by taking into account terrain traversability, thereby reducing frequent altitude changes and enabling smoother exploration. Extensive experiments conducted in both simulated and real-world environments demonstrate the effectiveness and advantages of our approach over existing solutions. Our approach demonstrates fast exploration of over 2000~$\text{m}^2$ of cluttered forest and sloped mountainous terrain with elevation changes of up to 10~m, reaching a maximum speed of 5~m/s in real-world tests.

authors.name: Mingyang Li
authors.institution: Chinese Academy of Medical Sciences & Peking Union Medical College

authors.name: Yi Luo
authors.institution: University of Science and Technology of China

papers.title: Adapting AI Weather Foundation Models to a Changing Climate
papers.abstract: AI weather foundation models learn from historical archives, while the climate distribution encountered during deployment continues to evolve. This growing model--climate mismatch motivates continual adaptation without repeated full-model retraining, but the structure of weather forecast errors determines how such adaptation should be performed. We develop an online adaptation framework that exploits two complementary error structures: geographically persistent biases and flow-dependent errors that vary with the atmospheric state. Analysis of Aurora-1.3B reveals strongly concentrated forecast-loss sensitivity in its decoder, motivating flow-dependent corrections within fixed low-dimensional sensitivity subspaces. A residual memory tracks persistent errors remaining after this correction, while a variable-wise online gate controls the contribution of the persistent component. We evaluate Aurora-1.3B using ERA5 from 1959--1968 for offline initialization and a strictly chronological 1969--2022 stream for online evaluation, with updates restricted to previously available verification targets. For 2-metre temperature, distributional departure from the historical reference, measured directly from ERA5, is associated with larger frozen-model errors and greater adaptation gains, while the adapted model maintains more stable skill across evaluation periods. Across 69 output fields and five lead times from 6 to 72 hours, our method reduces MSE and MAE by 6.90\% and 6.45\%, respectively, relative to $\delta$-Adapter, the strongest of six online adaptation baselines.

papers.title: Loop-OPF: Solver-Informed Learning for Optimal Power Flow with Inference-Time Topology Adaptivity
papers.abstract: Learning for optimal power flow (OPF) has recently been advocated to accelerate OPF solutions by using a pre-trained neural network (NN) to predict directly from given inputs such as the load demand. However, existing learning-for-OPF methods largely fall short of ensuring the optimality and feasibility of their predictions. They also struggle to adapt at inference time to unseen topology scenarios, such as those caused by line or generator outages. This work puts forth Loop-OPF, a solver-informed NN that builds its layers from the iterations of the primal-dual hybrid gradient (PDHG) method. Under standard convexity and regularity conditions on DC-OPF, the resultant fixed-point output of Loop-OPF is thus optimal and feasible. To speed up PDHG across diverse OPF scenarios, Loop-OPF learns certain PDHG parameters in a self-supervised manner, without any OPF solution labels. We adopt the deep equilibrium (DEQ) framework for training so that the memory cost does not grow with the number of layers. As the grid topology enters every layer as an input, the same trained Loop-OPF directly adapts to unseen contingencies without retraining. Numerical tests on the IEEE 300-bus and PEGASE 1354-, 2869-, and 9241-bus networks have demonstrated the accuracy and topology adaptivity of the proposed Loop-OPF over competing learning-for-OPF methods.

authors.name: Mohamad Chehade
authors.institution: The University of Texas at Austin

authors.name: Hao Zhu
authors.institution: Xi'an University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Trust and Lottery-Related Anomalies
papers.abstract: We examine whether social trust shapes the pricing of lottery-like stocks by influencing investors' beliefs regarding optimistic information associated with extreme future payoffs. We argue that higher social trust reduces investors' skepticism toward optimistic information associated with extreme future payoffs, increasing demand for lottery-type stocks and leading to overpricing and lower subsequent returns. Using a sample of 8,875 firms across 49 US states over the period 1996-2018 and MAX as a proxy for lottery-like characteristics, we show that the MAX effect is concentrated in regions with relatively high trust and is weak or absent in regions with relatively low trust. We further find that this trust conditioning is stronger in regions with lower education or income levels, consistent with social trust playing a relatively more important role when investors have more limited access to private information. The results are robust to alternative lottery proxies and a range of robustness checks. Our findings identify social trust as a novel determinant of the pricing of lottery-like stocks and provide evidence that social capital may amplify belief-driven mispricing in assets with highly skewed payoffs.

authors.name: Ya Gao
authors.institution: Xi’an University of Posts and Telecommunications

papers.title: HermiteTwin: Bicubic Hermite Shell Digital Twins for Contact-Rich Deformable Manipulation
papers.abstract: While existing methods for reconstructing deformable object manipulation have made impressive progress, they typically represent a thin object with a single particle set that must serve two purposes at once: modeling bending, and resolving contact with the robot. To bridge this gap, we present HermiteTwin, a framework that reconstructs a physical digital twin of a thin deformable object from multiview video of a robot manipulating it. Our key idea is to represent deformation and contact separately, each at its own resolution. The object is simulated as a bicubic Hermite shell, a coarse grid of $C^1$ elements whose nodal positions and derivatives define a smooth surface with Kirchhoff--Love bending, while the gripper acts through dense samples in material space that are captured, clamped, and released, and whose attachment forces reach the shell through the Hermite basis. This decoupling keeps the physical state compact while contact stays fine-grained. We identify effective material and contact parameters with CMA-ES followed by adjoint-based refinement, and drive a reconstructed Gaussian appearance model with the simulated shell. In experiments on real cloth and foam manipulation, HermiteTwin outperforms the state-of-the-art spring--mass twin across reconstruction, resimulation, and future prediction.

papers.title: Interstellar extinction estimates for nearly 90 million stars based on synthetic photometry from Gaia XP spectra
papers.abstract: Accurate stellar extinction measurements are essential for recovering intrinsic stellar properties and investigating the three-dimensional distribution of interstellar dust. We present reddening estimates for 87,270,425 stars using synthetic SMSS gri photometry derived from corrected Gaia DR3 XP spectra, combined with Gaia BP and RP, 2MASS JHKs, and WISE W1 photometry. Stellar extinction is determined through empirical SED fitting based on reference stellar loci constructed separately for dwarfs and giants. Comparisons with three external extinction catalogs show good overall agreement, with dispersions of 0.049-0.075 mag in E(B-V). The catalog covers approximately 99.99% of the sky. Using stars with sigma_d/d < 0.2, we further construct reddening maps in four distance ranges from 0 to 5 kpc, revealing prominent molecular clouds and large-scale Galactic dust structures. Extinction-corrected color-absolute-magnitude diagrams show significantly tighter stellar sequences and consistent red-clump features in different Galactic fields. The resulting catalog provides a homogeneous data set for stellar extinction correction and studies of Galactic dust structure.

authors.name: Bao-Kun Sun
authors.institution: University of Science and Technology of China

papers.title: A general reduction and explicit remoteness formulas for exact slow 2-Nim
papers.abstract: In exact slow $2$-Nim, a move removes one token from each of two nonempty piles. For any number of piles, we relate Smith remoteness in the exact game to the remoteness $D$ of Moore's slow game on the piles that remain after a largest pile is removed. If the total number of tokens $N$ is odd, the exact game has remoteness $\min(D,\lfloor N/2\rfloor)$. If $N$ is even, its remoteness equals $D$ when $2D\le N$ and is either $N/2$ or $N/2-1$ otherwise. Both values can occur for the same $N$, $D$, and number of piles. We determine $D$ explicitly for five piles. This gives a six-pile remoteness formula and a rule for selecting an optimal move. Both take $O(b)$ bit operations when each pile size has at most $b$ bits. We also give a closed formula for positions with any number of unit piles and two further piles of arbitrary size. For the GM move rule, we prove the proposed descriptions of the exceptions in the four- and five-pile games and give the exact threshold at which a specified six-pile move ceases to be optimal as the largest pile grows. Finally, we classify all outcome-preserving sorted translations for five and six piles.

authors.name: Raul Sanchez Galan
authors.institution: Nanjing University of Information Science and Technology

papers.title: EcomWriteBench: A Real-World Benchmark for E-commerce Writing Tasks
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used throughout e-commerce workflows to generate content that informs purchasing decisions and supports customer interactions. Evaluating these systems requires accounting for user needs, product evidence, structural constraints, and business requirements that are not fully captured by general-purpose writing benchmarks. We introduce EcomWriteBench, a real-world benchmark containing 3,861 queries from 69 e-commerce writing tasks across 13 categories and five languages. Through task-level extraction, cross-task consolidation, and refinement guided by human feedback, EcomWriteBench constructs a shared pool of 37 abilities and identifies the subset applicable to each task. Ability-wise scoring enables us to compare state-of-the-art LLMs on EcomWriteBench and characterize their relative strengths and weaknesses across fine-grained e-commerce writing abilities. We further propose a preference-calibrated weight-learning framework that converts human pairwise preferences into interpretable scoring rubrics through global, category-level, and task-level aggregation weights. This framework provides a reusable approach for translating human preferences into automated evaluation by combining ability discovery, ability-wise scoring, and preference-calibrated aggregation, and can potentially be applied to a broad range of benchmarks beyond EcomWriteBench. On held-out queries, our scoring framework achieves 88.96% agreement with human preferences, compared with 78.54% for conventional LLM-as-a-judge scoring.

authors.name: Feng Wang
authors.institution: Harbin University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Verifying and Strengthening Neural Tangent Kernel Theory
papers.abstract:
Writing
  Neural tangent kernel (NTK) theory explains why very wide neural networks trained by gradient methods converge in the lazy-training regime. Its standard proof combines matrix concentration, random Gram matrices, continuous-time dynamics, spectral perturbation, and a bootstrap argument, but has lacked machine-checked verification. We present a Lean\~4 formalisation for two-layer networks, proving an end-to-end theorem: for a smooth bounded activation (instantiated with $\sigma=\tanh$), frozen biases, paired $\pm 1$ initialisation, and explicit width conditions, gradient flow exists uniquely with probability at least $1-\delta$, and
  $$ \|r(t)\|^2 \leq \|y\|^2 e^{-\lambda_0 t/2}. $$
  The sole data assumption is population NTK non-degeneracy, $\lambda_0>0$. Initial coercivity, kernel drift, the movement bootstrap, the residual ODE, and flow existence and uniqueness are formally proved.
  The formalisation also sharpens the standard analysis in two ways. First, replacing the conventional matrix-Bernstein variance proxy with the classical row-covariance proxy yields estimated concentration-width certificates for $\tanh$ that are $36$--$53\times$ smaller at $(m,d)=(16,8)$ and $94$--$121\times$ smaller at $(32,16)$. Lean certifies the inequality; the ratios are numerical. Second, the network Hessian has operator norm $\Theta(\sqrt{p})$ on the sup-norm parameter ball (a paper calculation), preventing the expected $O(1/\sqrt{p})$ linearisation bound via sup-norm Taylor estimates. An $L^2$ parameter geometry resolves this issue. Required widths remain polynomial but far beyond practical scales, limiting applicability.

authors.name: Hao Zhu
authors.institution: Xi'an University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Abstract What Varies, Reuse Longer Patterns: Efficient Offline Chain-of-Thought Compression
papers.abstract: Offline chain-of-thought (CoT) compression creates shorter supervision for efficient reasoning, but per-example compressors repeatedly process similar expressions across traces, wasting compressor budget. Methods that reuse identical text across examples miss longer shared expressions when names, numbers, or formulas change from one question to another. We introduce CRAFT, which abstracts problem-specific details into slots to uncover partially lexicalized expression templates (PLETs) and clusters wording variants into families. Compressing each family representative once yields shared deletion or rewriting edits, which are applied with each occurrence's own details to construct compact, ordinary-text training targets. Compared with per-example rewriting, CRAFT Rewrite reduces weighted compressor budgets by a median 90.7% with a median accuracy loss of 1.21 percentage points, while generating shorter reasoning. Against cross-sample encoding, it shortens reasoning across all eight model-dataset settings by 25.3% on average and improves accuracy in five.

authors.name: Yifeng Zhao
authors.institution: Xi'an University of Science and Technology

authors.name: Hanzhang Zhou
authors.institution: Agency for Science, Technology and Research

papers.title: Can Vision-Language Models Synthesize Executable Game-Playing Programs?
papers.abstract: Recent advances in vision-language models (VLMs) have endowed multimodal agents with increasingly strong visual perception and long-horizon reasoning capabilities, making VLM-based autonomous game playing feasible. Existing game benchmarks primarily evaluate whether an agent can select appropriate actions from the current visual state across different scenarios and games. However, most of them adopt a step-by-step interaction paradigm where the current visual observation is sent to the agent before each action. In practical deployment, this paradigm introduces two fundamental limitations: the game loop must wait for model inference, making real-time interaction impractical, and repeated VLM calls incur substantial cost. Therefore, we propose PlayScriptBench, a script-based game benchmark that evaluates whether VLMs can synthesize an executable game-playing program from game states. This setting jointly evaluates visual grounding, understanding of game dynamics, long-horizon strategic reasoning, and executable program synthesis, providing a more comprehensive assessment of game-playing agents. To support more tractable evaluation for current general-purpose VLMs, we further introduce a four-stage pipeline --- Explore, Perception, API Construction, and Strategy Composition --- that decomposes controller synthesis into game exploration, state perception, interface construction, and strategic control, enabling agents to progressively construct an executable program. Experiments on 16 games spanning 4 genres show that even strong VLMs struggle on our benchmark, revealing a substantial gap between passive visual game understanding and executable closed-loop game control. These results establish script-based controller synthesis as a complementary direction for benchmarking VLM-based game-playing agents.

authors.name: Yao Tong
authors.institution: Second Affiliated Hospital of Xi'an Jiaotong University

authors.name: Jianqiang Huang
authors.institution: Chongqing University of Posts and Telecommunications

papers.title: Testing Settlement Flags after Late Evidence and Process Restart
papers.abstract: A settlement flag can survive an application restart while the economic effects remain ambiguous. We define a contract linking the fixed plan, source admission at two cutoffs, identity-keyed ledger effects and post-invocation state. We generated 504 synthetic histories, ran each through a file implementation and a separately coded SQLite implementation, and observed 672 controlled process exits. The file implementation missed 54 same-identity payment-date conflicts, including 27 that credited cash early, and a monitor using run flags, artifact presence and purchase counts accepted all 54. The same contract distinguishes a purchase awaiting closure from a correct quote wait for a single writer on a running kernel and filesystem.

papers.title: Which Archived Results Survive a Rule Change? A Case Study in Revalidating Decisions
papers.abstract: A research workflow can retain a correct numerical result after the evidence or approval that supported its use has expired. Common incremental build methods identify reusable computations, while deciding what remains usable also requires knowing which policy justified each approval. We examined a recorded parser migration across 312 paired research records, replayed both parsers with the same inputs, applied a calculation-file omission to the complete cohort, and evaluated current proof in a GNU Make comparison. Treating the prior projections as current would change at least one field in 11 of 312 records, and controlled cases show that even matching values can lack a current proof. The study separates numerical recovery from applicable approval and sets out the conditions under which a maintained dependency graph can preserve both.

papers.title: CoEvoBench: Can LLMs Drive Recursive Co-Evolution of Agentic Systems?
papers.abstract: The performance of an LLM agent depends on both its model and its harness, the code that mediates its interaction with tools and environments. Can LLM researchers drive this co-evolution as a recursive improvement process, deciding round after round which component to change when each change alters the value of the other? Existing benchmarks evaluate post-training or data research with the harness out of scope, or harness optimization with the model fixed, leaving this joint decision unmeasured. We introduce CoEvoBench, a benchmark that evaluates LLMs as researchers co-evolving the model and harness of a target agent across five agentic domains. Researchers start from a common base model and initial harness, train and revise within a 24-hour budget, and submit a model-harness pair that is scored on separate test tasks. Across five frontier researchers, the strongest closes more than four fifths of the gap to an instruction-tuned reference system, and co-evolution succeeds on interaction tasks but rarely on long-horizon coding. These results suggest that current LLMs can make a strong first improvement, but cannot yet turn feedback from an improved system into the next one. CoEvoBench provides a controlled testbed for measuring the research capabilities that recursive co-evolution requires.

authors.name: Chuan Xiao
authors.institution: China Academy Of Machinery Science & Technology (China)

papers.title: Learning Interaction Dynamics via Motion-Region Guidance for Robotic Video World Models
papers.abstract: Action-conditioned video world models imagine future observations under candidate robot actions, providing a promising visual tool for robot policy evaluation and interaction simulation. However, existing video world models often optimize global reconstruction errors instead of emphasizing interaction-relevant regions. As a result, they may preserve overall scene appearance but overlook local interaction details, leading to physically implausible outcomes such as hallucinated contact effects and inconsistent robot-object interactions. We introduce MoReWorld, a unified motion-region-guided framework that uses a shared motion region, the part of the environment that moves in response to the robot's actions, to focus dynamics learning and video generation on interaction-relevant regions. The same motion region guides local motion prediction, region-aware supervision, and motion-gated future-feature conditioning. At inference time, the motion region is predicted as a motion probability map from visual history and robot actions, without requiring future observations or ground-truth motion labels. On WorldSimProbe, MoReWorld achieves the highest overall simulator-faithfulness score, with the strongest performance on local consistency, global consistency, and interaction dynamics. These results indicate that motion-region guidance helps the model preserve scene-level consistency while more faithfully predicting action-conditioned interaction dynamics.

papers.title: Endpoint Exclusion for Bounded Damping on the Standard Flat Two-Torus
papers.abstract: We prove that, for every fixed nonzero nonnegative bounded damping $W$ on the standard flat two-torus, the stationary damped wave operator satisfies $\|(-\Delta-s^2+isW)^{-1}\|_{L^2\to L^2}=o(|s|)$. Consequently, for initial data in $H^2\times H^1$, the uniform decay rate of the square root of the energy improves from $O(t^{-1/2})$ to $o(t^{-1/2})$. This excludes the endpoint quasimodes proposed by Kleinhenz in 2024. The proof combines a uniform $L^4$ estimate, equidistribution of densities when the largest Fourier coefficient tends to zero, and a one-dimensional equation for a nonzero modulated weak limit. No continuity of the damping is required. The improvement may depend on $W$ and does not assert a fixed gain in the polynomial exponent.

papers.title: A Proof of a P\'olya--Szeg\H{o} Conjecture: A PDE Approach to Capacity Inequalities
papers.abstract:
We prove a planar capacity-ratio inequality conjectured by Polya and Szego, together with its extension to adjacent dimensions: for every integer $n\geq2$ and compact set $K\subset\mathbb{R}^n$, $C_{n-1}(K)\leq \left[ rac{\Gamma(n/2)}{\sqrt\pi \Gamma((n+1)/2)}ight]^{1/(n-1)}C_{n-2}(K),$ where $C_s$ denotes the length-homogeneous Riesz capacity and, when $n=2$, $C_{n-2}=C_0$ is logarithmic capacity. Closed balls attain equality, so the constant is sharp. Starting from an exterior Dirichlet problem and its nonnegative boundary flux, we construct a function $ho$ in one higher dimension, with coordinates $X=(x,z)$, and prove that, for $z
e0$, $\Deltaho= rac{n-1}{ho}|
ablaho|^2+ rac{ho_z}{z}, \quad ho|
ablaho|^2\leq(ho^2-1) rac{ho_z}{z}.$ A decreasing function $\Phi_n$ solving a suitable ordinary differential equation makes $U=\Phi_n(ho)$ superharmonic outside the conductor. Green's formula on the exterior of level sets of $U$ then bounds the Dirichlet integral by the total flux at infinity, and the Dirichlet principle yields the capacity bound. Smooth outer approximation extends the result to arbitrary compact sets. The same construction, combined with a comparison principle for weighted elliptic equations, gives the sharp upper bound for $C_q/C_{n-2}$ when $n-2<q<n$.

papers.title: Exploring Early Vulnerability Analysis via Automatic Identification of Vulnerability-Introducing Commits
papers.abstract: Developing effective vulnerability analysis techniques requires high-quality datasets that capture how vulnerabilities appear and evolve in real software codebase. Existing datasets, however, typically label as vulnerable only the code immediately preceding vulnerability-fixing commits (VFCs), overlooking the earlier versions in which vulnerabilities were first introduced and subsequently evolved. This practice limits both dataset coverage and our understanding of whether current detectors can identify vulnerabilities during their early, latent stages. In this paper, we present three manually annotated datasets of vulnerability-introducing commits (VICs) based on recent CVEs and widely used open-source projects. We further propose D-SZZ, a data state-aware VIC identification framework that analyzes security-fixing patterns and performs vulnerability scope slicing to recover the semantics implied by a fix. Experimental results demonstrate that D-SZZ outperforms existing SZZ and LLM-based baselines in identifying VICs. In addition, we evaluate six representative vulnerability detectors and find that models trained only on pre-VFC code struggle with original vulnerabilities, while incorporating early-stage samples improves detection performance. We also show that D-SZZ improves downstream vulnerable-version identification, and use it to uncover 16 inaccurate affected-version records in the NVD, all of which were officially confirmed and updated.

authors.name: Youpeng Li
authors.institution: The University of Texas at Dallas

authors.name: Xinda Wang
authors.institution: China University of Mining and Technology - Beijing

papers.title: FORTH: Grounding Tactile VLA Execution via Forward-Only Proxy-Control Pairing
papers.abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) policies are widely credited with force control, operating on the unverified assumption that proxy loss minimization implies physical force grounding. In this work, we demonstrate that this assumption breaks down at three core deployment levels: frozen visual backbones discard contact geometry, downstream losses mask token-level gradient alignment, and discrete indicators trigger optimization collapse. To address these disconnections, we present FORTH, a forward-only measurement harness and execution framework that explicitly pairs the optimization objective at each level with its physical control observable. FORTH incorporates three grounded pillars: a layer-local, forward-only tactile encoder that preserves spatial contact geometry without backpropagation, a token-parallel zeroth-order adapter enabling activation-space updates, and SlipGuard, a continuous tactile verification gate that fires on incipient slip. On an elasto-plastic structural shell, FORTH's closed-loop gate peaks at 29 times lower grip force than a monotone reflex ramp, preventing structural crush where the baseline leaves permanent deformation. Furthermore, FORTH matches state-of-the-art execution performance with a 97.6% average success rate across three evaluated LIBERO suites, while reducing peak activation memory by 7.12 times compared to a backpropagated step on the same backbone. Enhanced perception enables deeper physical intelligence.

authors.name: Yaoxin Li
authors.institution: University of Science and Technology of China

papers.title: LEAN: Library-Based Adaptation for Asynchronous, Federated Fine-Tuning
papers.abstract: Federated fine-tuning of foundation models with low-rank adapters (LoRA) is typically reconciled by averaging locally trained adapters. In cross-device settings, where participants hold heterogeneous data and join or leave asynchronously, averaging is poorly suited: locally trained adapters are not identifiable up to permutation, and averages of adapters trained on dissimilar data can be uninformative or unstable. We propose a simple idea called federated library-based adaptation (LEAN), which replaces averaging altogether. The server maintains a library of rank-1 basis pairs; participants check out random subsets, fine-tune them locally as a LoRA adapter, and check them back in, so that each pair is shuffled across sites and trained on many participants' data. Because no aggregation step is required, LEAN operates fully asynchronously and communicates only low-rank parameters. We prove that, in a synchronous setting, LEAN converges to a neighborhood of a stationary point, with the shuffle canceling data heterogeneity at first order.
