Across image and text fine-tuning benchmarks, LEAN outperforms averaging-based baselines in most settings with substantially less communication, and remains effective under heavy data heterogeneity, where averaging-based methods fail to reach nontrivial accuracy, and under heavy asynchrony, where they degrade substantially.

authors.name: Zhimin Ding
authors.institution: Liaoning Institute of Science and Technology

authors.name: Yuxin Tang
authors.institution: Harbin University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Scoliosis5K: Multimodal Gait Analysis via Clip-Conditioned RGB-Silhouette Fusion
papers.abstract: Color walking video records body boundary motion alongside clothing folds, surface appearance, and recording-environment cues. To examine what an explicit binary silhouette contributes to participant-level classification of scoliosis-related gait when a classifier already observes the paired color sequence, we construct Scoliosis5K, a multi-site collection of 4,998 corridor-walking sequences across 3,010 participant identifiers in which RGB person crops, binary silhouettes, and two-dimensional poses share each recording identifier and frame index. Our architecture uses each patch's pixel deviation from its clip mean to weight two low-rank query and value updates inside a pretrained RGB encoder, fusing the resulting video representation with a silhouette transformer sequence and regional kernel ridge scores extracted from one native-resolution RGB frame per window. Across 988 participants in five participant-disjoint cross-validation folds and three training seeds, the complete system reaches 83.77% accuracy and 79.91% macro-averaged F1, compared with 83.27% accuracy and 79.56% macro-F1 when the video RGB encoder remains frozen under identical inputs. Zeroing the silhouette vector at fixed weights shifts overall accuracy by only 0.10 percentage points while raising positive-category recall from 68.52% to 77.78% and lowering recall for both remaining categories. Macro-averaged AUROC is 0.950 across the cohort and 0.879 among participant pairs matched on acquisition site and recording-count group.

authors.name: Zizhao Peng
authors.institution: Southern University of Science and Technology

authors.name: Fengwei An
authors.institution: Southern University of Science and Technology

papers.title: The double-endpoint Strichartz estimate for dispersion-managed Schr\"odinger equations
papers.abstract: We adapt the near-far argument of Hadama and Toyoshima to establish the double-endpoint Strichartz estimate for dispersion-managed Schr\"odinger equations.

authors.name: Jiqiang Zheng
authors.institution: Institute of Applied Physics and Computational Mathematics

papers.title: Yau's first eigenvalue conjecture for embedded minimal hypersurfaces with constant scalar curvature
papers.abstract: Let $M^n$ be a smooth closed connected embedded minimal hypersurface of the unit sphere. Suppose that $M$ has constant scalar curvature. We prove that its first positive Laplace eigenvalue is $n$ and that the ambient coordinate functions span its first eigenspace. To prove both assertions, we consider an eigenfunction $f$ with eigenvalue $0<\lambda\le n$ orthogonal to every coordinate function. We use $f$ as the density of a single-layer potential on the sphere. The geometry of $M$ gives a lower bound for the Dirichlet energy of this potential. The spherical heat kernel gives a smaller upper bound for the same energy. This contradiction rules out every such nonzero $f$.

papers.title: Budget-Aware Predict-and-Verify Theorem Proving with Heterogeneous LLM Solvers
papers.abstract:
Large language model (LLM) theorem solvers differ in both proving capability and inference cost. Applying an expensive solver to every subgoal wastes computation when cheaper models are sufficient, while always starting from the cheapest solver wastes attempts on subgoals that require stronger models. We present BudgetPV, an agentic budget-aware predict-and-verify system that allocates computation across unresolved subgoals and heterogeneous LLM solvers. BudgetPV uses a cross-solver predictor to guide solver selection for each subgoal and revises the allocation as verification feedback becomes available.
  The allocation problem changes as proving progresses. Early decisions mainly determine which solver should handle an untried subgoal, while later decisions determine which previously attempted subgoals should receive additional computation. We train the predictor with two objectives for these two stages. Class-weighted cross-entropy improves assignment to less frequent stronger solvers during the initial stage, while plain cross-entropy provides better calibrated probabilities for later allocation among previously attempted subgoals.
  We evaluate BudgetPV on Lean Workbook, miniF2F, ProofNet, and PutnamBench using three progressively expanded solver settings: a strong but expensive solver alone, adding a medium-cost solver with intermediate solving capability, and further adding a cheap solver with lower solving capability. BudgetPV requires less LLM generation computation than uniform allocation to solve the same number of subgoals across the evaluated settings. The experiments further show the computation savings obtained as medium- and lower-cost solvers are added.

authors.name: Wei Jiang
authors.institution: Harbin University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Semigroup Hessian Estimates for Underdamped Langevin Dynamics
papers.abstract:
For the semigroup $e^{t\mathcal L}$ of the underdamped Langevin dynamics, we bound the Hessian $
abla^2(e^{t\mathcal L}f)$ when $
abla f$ is uniformly bounded. When the potential is strongly convex outside a ball and has bounded second and third derivatives, and the damping rate is above an explicit threshold, the bounds on $
abla^2(e^{t\mathcal L}f)$ decay exponentially in time with constants free of the dimension. The proof combines the Wasserstein contraction of the dynamics with a Bismut--Elworthy--Li formula for the degenerate noise. As an application, we prove the uniform-in-time error of the stochastic gradient UBU integrator, with an explicit coefficient of the numerical bias in the step size, proportional to the covariance of the stochastic gradient noise.

papers.title: PIU-CR: Physics-Informed Deep Unfolding with SAR-Optical Image Fusion for Cloud Removal
papers.abstract: Multi-modal cloud removal exploits complementary optical and synthetic aperture radar (SAR) images to restore cloud-degraded remote sensing images. Most existing methods rely on black-box, data-driven architectures with limited interpretability of cross-modal interactions. Although some attempts introduce physical priors into networks, their oversimplified formulations fail to faithfully characterize the underlying physical imaging process and the networks remain loosely coupled with optimization variables. To address these issues, we propose a physics-informed deep unfolding network for cloud removal via optical-SAR image fusion, termed as PIU-CR. We first formulate cloud removal as a physics-informed optimization problem. Specifically, we fundamentally ground the optimization in the physical imaging mechanism of cloud degradation by embedding the atmospheric scattering model into the data fidelity term. Then, the regularization terms establish an explicit cross-modal interaction mechanism, overcoming the single-modal information scarcity and the obscure, uninterpretable interactions in black-box models. They are dedicated to SAR-guided structure and spectral regularization, jointly introducing cross-modal structural feature alignment and coordinated spectral consistency constraints. The resulting optimization problem is then unfolded into a multi-stage neural network with dedicated structure and spectral branches. Each stage corresponds to an explicit optimization iteration step, enabling interpretable and effective reconstruction process. Experiments demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms state-of-the-art methods. The code is publicly available at https://github.com/Fgq188/PIU_CR.

authors.name: Han Xu
authors.institution: Heilongjiang University of Science and Technology

authors.name: Junxi Li
authors.institution: Ministry of Emergency Management of the People's Republic of China

papers.title: A Plan or an Adversarial Example? A Round-Trip Check for Latent World Models
papers.abstract: If we optimize an image until a classifier is confident it shows a cat, we may get an adversarial example, not a cat. Planning with a latent world model is a similar search for actions whose predicted future is closest to the goal. Is the result a plan, or an adversarial example of the world model? We show that it can be either. On the released DINO-WM and LeWM, more iterations of the cross-entropy method (CEM) lower the predicted cost but lose up to half of the problems CEM had already solved. The model's own predictions do not reveal these failures. We propose a simple test that executes the plan after every iteration and counts the problems a planner solves and then loses. Unlike an image, a plan comes with its actions, which our round-trip check reads back from the predicted states with a small network, penalizing mismatches. The check reads back the sum of each block of five actions, the part that two consecutive predicted states determine. Without retraining the world model and at only 0.2% to 3.1% more planning time, it improves the widely used planners CEM and MPPI on three released world models, and gains more where planners lose more problems. Without replanning, success rises from 0.39 to 0.76 on Wall with DINO-WM and from 0.56 to 0.94 for MPPI on JEPA-WM. With replanning (MPC), it rises from 0.70 to 0.81 on Cube with LeWM.

papers.title: Recoverable Necking Enabled by Reverse Phase-Boundary Motion in Liquid Crystal Elastomers
papers.abstract: Strain localization is often associated with plastic flow and permanent deformation. Here we show that a tensile neck in a crosslinked nematic network can undergo nearly complete recovery through reverse phase-boundary motion, leaving little residual deformation. In a monodomain liquid crystal elastomer stretched perpendicular to its initial director, this recovery occurs during an isothermal loading-unloading cycle. Digital image correlation resolves the process as the retreat of interfaces separating low- and high-stretch regions, where the high-stretch domain shrinks while previously necked material thickens, despite substantial mechanical hysteresis. Within the recoverable-necking regime, increasing temperature lowers the loading plateau stress but raises the unloading plateau stress. A nonconvex constitutive description provides an energetic basis for the coexistence of the two stretch states, while gradient regularization accounts for the finite width of their interfaces through an equilibrium reference profile. These results identify the spatial mechanism of neck recovery and distinguish recoverable strain localization from mechanical reversibility in an orientationally ordered polymer network.

papers.title: Improved Accuracy Scaling with Problem Complexity in LLM Arithmetic Reasoning Using Executable Symbolic Representations
papers.abstract: High accuracy on mathematical benchmarks does not establish whether reasoning remains reliable as problem complexity increases. We examine how executable symbolic representations change accuracy scaling in large language models compared with natural-language reasoning. To address this limitation, we introduce the GSM Arithmetic Benchmark (GSM-AB), a controlled benchmark that independently varies operand digit length and operation count to probe numerical scale and compositional complexity. We find that executable representations can improve accuracy and slow its decline as complexity increases. Lean reduces average sensitivity to operand digit length at every tested model size. By contrast, slower degradation with increasing operation count emerges at the larger model sizes. A Python program-of-thought (Python-PoT) control shows a similar operation-axis pattern, suggesting that this finding is not specific to Lean. These findings show that reasoning representation shapes arithmetic accuracy scaling and support executable symbolic representations for more reliable reasoning on complex arithmetic tasks.

authors.name: Shi-Ju Ran
authors.institution: Chinese Academy of Medical Sciences & Peking Union Medical College

papers.title: Revealing the growth of structural length in glass-forming liquids without using dynamical information
papers.abstract: Dynamical heterogeneity underlies the dramatic slowdown of supercooled liquids and has long been a central topic in glass physics. Despite considerable progress in identifying structural motifs and order parameters correlated with dynamical heterogeneity, a general characterization of structural descriptors remains elusive because they can vary among glass formers and are not generally known \emph{a priori}. To address this challenge, we establish a unified framework that can be applied to varieties of glass formers to extract structural signatures of dynamical heterogeneity directly from their static configurations. The framework combines a graph neural network (GNN) with gradient-weighted class activation mapping (Grad-CAM). Across three canonical three-dimensional glass-forming models, the resulting structural field exhibits a characteristic correlation length that tracks the corresponding dynamical correlation length. Notably, a network trained on small systems can be applied to larger systems without retraining, indicating that the extracted features are encoded in local and mesoscopic structural correlations. These results demonstrate that static configurations encode structural signatures of dynamical heterogeneity and establish a scalable, interpretable route for extracting them.

authors.name: Yusuke Hara
authors.institution: National Institute of Advanced Industrial Science and Technology

authors.name: Norihiro Oyama
authors.institution: Toyota Central Research and Development Laboratories (Japan)

papers.title: User-Irrepressible Sequences for Multiple-Packet Reception
papers.abstract: This paper studies deterministic transmission schemes based on protocol sequences for slot-synchronous multiple-packet reception (MPR) channels without feedback or synchronization of sequence phases. Each user schedules its transmissions according to a preassigned periodic binary sequence. A sequence set has the user-irrepressible property with MPR capability $\gamma$ ($\gamma$-UI) if every user is guaranteed at least one successful transmission per period, regardless of the relative cyclic shifts. We propose a unified explicit construction based on the Chinese Remainder Theorem (CRT) for arbitrary MPR capability $\gamma\geq 2$. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first unified CRT-based construction framework for $\gamma$-UI sequences over this full range, without requiring conflict-avoiding codes with prescribed parameters. We establish the $\gamma$-UI property through bounds on pairwise Hamming cross-correlations and show that suitably selected subsets support one additional active user without increasing the sequence length. We also derive exact average individual delay expressions over all possible cyclic shifts and extend the delay analysis to $\gamma$-UI sequence sets obtained from conflict-avoiding codes.

authors.name: Yuan-Hsun Lo
authors.institution: Chinese University of Hong Kong, Shenzhen

papers.title: Budgeted Safety Verification for Streaming Video Generation
papers.abstract: A streamed video generator releases each chunk the moment that it is produced, so a safety decision that waits for the finished clip arrives after the harm has been seen. We measure a guardrail by exposure, the harmful frames a viewer is shown, and ask where a fixed moderation budget should be spent. The accurate detector reads decoded frames with a video language model and is too expensive for every chunk, so our guard reads hidden states the generator has computed already and spends a cheap score on deciding when to call it. On 599 streams from a distilled causal generator the undefended model shows 46.25 harmful frames of 81. The video model on every chunk leaves 0.91 frames at 80.1 scored per benign stream, and the same model triggered by our guard leaves 2.35 at 5.3. Spending that budget at random leaves 37.20 frames, so the gain is in the ordering, and a frame detector in the same role gives up almost six, so the judging stage must read the chunk as a clip. The ordering is worth more as the stream lengthens, and the guard carries to a second system. An independent guardrail model agrees with our oracle at $\kappa=0.74$, and a blinded audit by 50 participants puts its precision at 96.1% and recall at 82.8%. Warning. This paper contains examples of generated content that some readers may find disturbing or offensive in nature.

authors.name: Xianglin Yang
authors.institution: Hunan University of Humanities, Science and Technology

papers.title: MODULE: A Mutual-Promoting Deep Unfolding Framework Towards Degradation-Robust Multi-modal Image Fusion
papers.abstract: Multi-modal image fusion is crucial for comprehensive scene representation, yet real-world degradations compromise its efficacy, necessitating degradation-robust fusion paradigms. Existing degradation-robust multi-modal image fusion methods are often hindered by cascaded sub-optimal solution or black-box opacity. To address these challenges, we propose a theory-inspired mutual-promoting deep unfolding framework. It reformulates degradation-robust image fusion as a joint optimization problem, utilizing the degradation model and modality generation mechanism to explicitly model both single-task priors and cross-task dependencies. By decomposing the complex multi-task optimization problem into task-related iterative subproblems, the framework establishes a bidirectional reciprocal information flow between restoration and fusion. This process is further unfolded into a multi-stage deep neural network, where each component explicitly corresponds to a specific mathematical operation. In our framework, the fused cross-modal prior actively regularizes the ill-posed restoration, while the purified modality features continuously refine the fusion output. It ensures a transparent architecture that combines the merits of both model-based and data-driven methodologies. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our paradigm achieves state-of-the-art performance while providing superior interpretability. The code is publicly available at https://github.com/Meskend/MODULE.

authors.name: Han Xu
authors.institution: Heilongjiang University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Suspected Until Inspected: Neuro-Symbolic Detection of Broken Access Control in Server-Side Web Applications
papers.abstract: Broken access control (BAC) has topped the OWASP Top 10 since 2021. Unfortunately, a decade of detectors still leaves a gap on every front. Static analyzers are tied to one language or framework, dynamic testers cover only the endpoints they manage to exercise, and LLM-based auditors leave the final verdict to an error-prone model. In this paper, we design and implement FLINT, a neuro-symbolic framework that detects BAC in server-side web applications without language- or framework-specific rules. Our key insight is to separate the proposal from the verdict -- an LLM may flag any data access as needing a guard, but only a symbolically verified check can clear it. The neural component enumerates every endpoint and distills each, via demand-driven code slicing, into an authorization certificate whose claims are all grounded in cited code. The symbolic component verifies each claimed check through origin tracing and a lattice-based interprocedural dataflow analysis, so that no access is cleared on the model's word. When applied to popular real-world open-source applications, including Gitea, Grafana, and Strapi, FLINT detected 112 zero-day, exploitable BAC vulnerabilities, 30 of them in projects with over 20,000 GitHub stars. We have responsibly disclosed all of them to the developers. Mattermost, for example, has already confirmed our report and is assigning a CVE identifier.

authors.name: Zifeng Kang
authors.institution: Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications

authors.name: Dongqi Han
authors.institution: Shanghai University of Traditional Chinese Medicine

authors.name: Shihong Zou
authors.institution: Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications

papers.title: The geometric expansion of the coarse trace formula of GL(4)
papers.abstract: We study the non-semisimple terms in the geometric side of Arthur's trace formula of $\rm{GL}(4)$ for the further study of the invariant trace formula. After modifying the zeta function and Arthur's definition of the weighted orbital integrals, we compare the two ways to calculate the distributions $J^T(f)$ of the geometric side, we can obtain that the distributions can be written as the linear combanition of the weighted orbital integrals. In particular, we get the coefficients $a^M(S,\gamma)$, for all $\gamma\in \rm{GL}(4,F)$, expressed by the measure and zeta functions.

authors.name: Xinghua Cui
authors.institution: Jiangxi University of Finance and Economics

authors.name: Zhifeng Peng
authors.institution: Henan University of Animal Husbandry and Economy

papers.title: Smoothed Conformal Testing with Small Calibration Sets
papers.abstract: A small calibration sample restricts split conformal $p$-values to a coarse rank grid. Randomization removes this discretization, but its effect depends on both the smoothing interval and the allocation of auxiliary random variables. Independent tie-block randomization is exactly valid under null exchangeability. When calibration and null scores are jointly exchangeable conditional on the alternative scores, we prove positive regression dependence and hence Benjamini--Hochberg false discovery rate control, including for atomic score distributions. Smoothing over calibration-dependent rank cells agrees with tie-block randomization when calibration scores are distinct and no test score ties a calibration score, but can fail marginal validity with atoms. Assigning sorted random draws according to score order can invalidate even a single null $p$-value. An exact two-test example violates the usual $\pi_0\alpha$ bound, and simulations with continuous scores exhibit false discovery rates above the nominal level $\alpha$. Finally, conditional moment identities and normal-model illustrations show that removing the rank grid does not remove calibration uncertainty. Randomization can produce additional discoveries, including when ordinary conformal testing cannot reject at all, but it does not generally substitute for a larger calibration sample.

authors.name: Mingzhou Deng
authors.institution: Academy of Mathematics and Systems Science

papers.title: H-MSAE: Hierarchical Sparse Concept Coverage for Efficient and Diverse Instruction Data Selection
papers.abstract: Large instruction-tuning corpora contain substantial semantic redundancy, motivating the selection of compact subsets that preserve useful supervision while reducing training cost. Existing diversity-aware selectors often rely on generated semantic tags and explicit graph structures, introducing considerable annotation and preprocessing overhead. We introduce H-MSAE, a hierarchical sparse instruction selection framework that organizes multi-resolution concepts learned by a Matryoshka sparse autoencoder into a coarse-to-fine hierarchy. Quality-weighted, diminishing-return coverage with ancestor propagation promotes high-quality and non-redundant semantic coverage, while pool-relative length constraints regulate subset composition. We motivate this design through a local quality-diversity analysis of subset SFT utility and examine it using example-quality and representation-space diversity diagnostics. On Tulu 3 data pool, H-MSAE achieves the highest Final Avg among the evaluated 50K selectors across scales and initialization. The selected subset also exhibits the highest mean quality and effective rank among the evaluated methods. By avoiding full-pool generative tagging and supporting efficient sparse selection, H-MSAE reduces measured end-to-end runtime by approximately $5\times$ relative to MIG.

authors.name: Feng Wang
authors.institution: Harbin University of Science and Technology

papers.title: A Validation-Driven Bilevel Optimization Method for Mesh-Free PDE Solvers and Its Error Analysis
papers.abstract: Mesh-free partial differential equation (PDE) solvers construct discrete systems from residuals at sampled points. These solvers fit coefficients in a parameterized trial representation and select solver-design parameters governing the representation, training-residual weighting, and regularization. These parameters strongly affect solution accuracy, yet existing selection strategies are largely tailored to particular solver classes. To address this limitation, we formulate a unified validation-driven bilevel optimization framework applicable across different solver classes, in which the lower level fits coefficients using training collocation residuals, while the upper level selects solver-design parameters using held-out validation residuals. For nonlinear PDEs, however, solving the nonlinear lower-level problem to high accuracy is costly, while the adjoint system is typically ill-conditioned and indefinite. To address this issue, we propose an efficient implicit hypergradient method that approximates the lower-level response using finite, warm-started damped Gauss-Newton (GN) updates. For the adjoint solve, we use the damped GN matrix to compute an initial adjoint and to precondition a finite number of minimum residual iterations. To quantify the errors introduced by these approximations, we derive local hypergradient error bounds that separate the contributions of the finite lower-level solve, adjoint damping, and the final adjoint residual. Combining this analysis with validation sampling bounds and residual stability, we relate validation residuals to PDE solution accuracy and establish error bounds for the computed PDE solution. Numerical experiments on several nonlinear PDEs, including a high-dimensional problem, demonstrate the accuracy and efficiency of the proposed method across Kansa, random feature and extreme learning machine, and physics-informed neural network solvers.

authors.name: Shangzhi Zeng
authors.institution: Southern University of Science and Technology

papers.title: AnyBodyCodec: A Shared Native Interface for Body-Model Conversion, Extension, and Humanoid Control
papers.abstract: Parametric body models expose incompatible pose and shape controls, tying humanoid policies to particular input formats. AnyBodyCodec learns a shared representation through native conversion, then reuses it for new body models and control with its core frozen. Encoders map MHR, SMPL-X, and SOMA to aligned slots; native decoders recover target controls. The 1.090M-parameter converter covers nine routes and reaches 16.801 mm input-reference MPJPE across six cross routes: the 2.887M Transformer bank reaches 16.390 mm and its parameter-matched version 18.866 mm. Three measured routes take 7.43-7.67 ms on an RTX 4090. Adding ANNY shows that comparable conversion accuracy can accompany different action consistency under one frozen controller. Under a matched PPO budget, aligned slots support 60.78% full-action success across three formats. Separate 160-hour training reaches 66.10% source-weighted validation success, and the controller is deployed qualitatively on a physical G1 through three visual front ends. Together, these results establish reuse through both native geometric fidelity and downstream policy compatibility.

papers.title: Beyond a Single Human Demonstration: Learning from Scored Trajectory Alternatives for End-to-End Driving
papers.abstract: Human driving logs record only one trajectory per scene, leaving other feasible driving choices without explicit trajectory targets or quality labels. This limits supervision for end-to-end planners that generate and refine multiple candidate trajectories. Meanwhile, conditioning refinement on a large vision-language model adds substantial online inference cost. We propose DriveSTA, which extends autoregressive proposal generation and proposal-conditioned residual flow refinement with scored trajectory alternatives. For each training scene, we generate alternatives offline through smooth deformations of the recorded trajectory and evaluate their simulated execution against logged traffic. Diverse, high-quality alternatives supervise distinct proposals and define residual targets for quality-guided denoising, while candidates spanning the full score range train a scorer to assess driving quality. A shared joint-embedding predictive architecture (JEPA), adapted through masked video-feature prediction, encodes observed frames once and provides temporal context for both refinement and scoring. On NAVSIM v1 Navtest, DriveSTA ranks first among the compared planners trained on NAVSIM data alone. With expanded training data, DriveSTA-Scale achieves state-of-the-art results among the compared methods on Navtest and closed-loop HUGSIM, while reducing mean planner forward-pass latency by 73% relative to ChainFlow-VLA in matched evaluations.

authors.name: Zheyuan Lai
authors.institution: Nanjing University of Aeronautics and Astronautics

papers.title: Forbidden T-symmetry breaking in time-dependent non-Hermitian systems with gain and loss
papers.abstract: Parity-time ($PT$) symmetry has attracted significant interest in photonics and related fields in recent years. With sufficiently weak gain and loss, these systems typically exhibit entirely real energy levels, with all corresponding wave functions remaining $PT$ symmetric. As the strength of gain and loss increases, complex-conjugate energy levels are expected to emerge, signaling the onset of $PT$ symmetry breaking. Similar properties can be found in non-Hermitian systems with other antilinear symmetries as well, where parity is replaced by another operator such as rotation ($R$) or simply the identity operator, resulting in $RT$-symmetric and $T$-symmetric non-Hermitian systems. In this work, we demonstrate that this typical scenario of non-Hermitian symmetry breaking in a finite Hilbert space is forbidden in a class of time-dependent systems with gain and loss and $T$ symmetry: the system remains in its $T$-symmetric phase as we increase the strength of gain and loss, even when the spatial distribution of gain and loss is random. Furthermore, this behavior is also independent of the duration or period of the temporal modulation. In contrast, this forbidden non-Hermitian symmetry breaking does not occur when the same systems are modified to display $PT$ symmetry instead. Our findings highlight contrasting behaviors in time-dependent and time-independent non-Hermitian systems, creating new possibilities and opportunities for future investigations.

papers.title: Essential norms of composition operators on Hardy spaces of homogeneous rooted trees
papers.abstract: We establish characterizations of the essential norms of composition operators on Hardy spaces of homogeneous rooted trees. As direct applications of our main results, we obtain compactness criteria for such composition operators.

papers.title: On Robust Strictly Positive Real Synthesis for High-Order Interval Polynomials
papers.abstract: We establish two complementary results on common strictly positive real (SPR) numerators for Hurwitz-stable interval polynomial families. First, for every order $n \ge 10$, we construct a monic Hurwitz-stable interval polynomial family with rational endpoints and positive width in every nonleading coefficient such that every nonzero real numerator of degree at most $n$ produces a strictly negative real part at some member and some positive frequency. In particular, robust Hurwitz stability alone does not guarantee equal-degree SPR synthesis in high orders. Second, for every order $n \ge 1$, we prove that a common real SPR numerator of exact degree $n$ always exists whenever the lower endpoint of each interior coefficient interval is at most $10^{-5}$ times its upper endpoint, while the constant and leading coefficients vary over arbitrary compact positive intervals.

authors.name: ZhengTai Xiong
authors.institution: Chongqing University of Posts and Telecommunications

authors.name: Long Wang
authors.institution: Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications

authors.name: Wensheng Yu
authors.institution: Changchun University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Extremal problems for graphs with bounded $k$-th binding number
papers.abstract:
The binding number of a graph, introduced by Woodall [J. Combin. Theory, Ser. B, 1973], is a central topic in structural and extremal graph theory. Recently, Chen et al. introduced the $k$-th binding number $\beta^k(G)$. Anderson [J. Combin. Theory, Ser. B, 1971] proved that every graph $G$ of even order with $\beta^1(G)\ge\frac43$ contains a perfect matching, and that the bound $\frac43$ is best possible. For $k\ge2$, Chen et al. proved that $\beta^k(G)\ge1$ guarantees a $k$-factor whenever $kn$ is even, and that the bound $1$ is best possible. The above facts reveal a fundamental distinction between the higher-order binding number and the classical binding number. This distinction makes extremal problems for graphs with bounded $k$-th binding number particularly intriguing.
  For positive integers $n,$ $k$ and $r$, we in this paper determine the maximum size and spectral radius among all graphs $G$ of order $n$ satisfying $\beta^k(G)<r$, and characterize the corresponding extremal graphs, respectively. In particular, when $k=1$, our results imply the corresponding extremal results of Fan and Lin [Electron. J. Combin., 2024] and Liu, Chen and Fan [Electron. J. Combin., 2026]. Our proofs develop a structural framework that relates higher-order neighborhood inequalities to the structure of the complements of graphs. This framework may provide an approach to Tur\'{a}n-type problem involving the $k$-th binding number, and the approach may be of independent interest.

authors.name: Ruifang Liu
authors.institution: Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications

papers.title: Riemannian Curvature Functionals for de Rham Spectral Triples
papers.abstract: We compute mixed Clifford residue functionals for the Hodge-de Rham operator in even dimensions. A symbol-composition calculation recovers the Riemann and Einstein tensors and yields two ordered curvature functionals with the same classical limit. For specified truncation products on warped collars, we evaluate all five boundary cases and prove that the curvature-recovering antisymmetrizations have no boundary correction. We extend the constructions to spectral data equipped with two one-form actions. Explicit noncommutative torus and finite-direction examples distinguish the functionals and exhibit failures of module balancing and Riemann symmetries. A conformal example shows that a naive exterior lift need not recover classical curvature. The additional structures and limitations of each extension are stated explicitly.

papers.title: Extremal $K_t$-intersecting graph families for large $t$
papers.abstract: In this paper, we show that for every sufficiently large positive integer $t$ and every integer $n \ge t$, every $K_t$-intersecting family $\mathcal{G}$ of graphs on vertex set $[n]$ has size at most $2^{\binom{n}{2}-\binom{t}{2}}$. Furthermore, when the equality is attained, $\mathcal{G}$ must consist of all graphs on $[n]$ that contain some fixed copy of $K_t$. Our result settles a conjecture of Ellis, Filmus, and Friedgut for sufficiently large $t$. We also present a short proof for the odd-cycle-intersecting case, slightly different from the existing proofs in the literature.

papers.title: BinXSight: Fast Binary Program Summarization via Hierarchical Modular Decomposition
papers.abstract: Binary code summarization (BCS) is crucial in fields such as cybersecurity. Particularly, program-level BCS can quickly provide a comprehensive overview of an entire stripped binary without in-depth manual reverse engineering. However, a binary often contains numerous functions with complex interactions, making it challenging to extract its functionality efficiently. Moreover, existing methods focus solely on function-level without considering contextual information, limiting their applicability to program-level analysis. Towards comprehensive and fast program-level BCS, we propose BinXSight, an LLM-powered framework based on hierarchical modular decomposition. Specifically, we first propose binary graph, a new data structure composed of four graphs, to comprehensively represent a binary. Then, based on the binary graph, we hierarchically decompose functions into modules and select the most significant ones. Finally, BinXSight generates a program-level summary from these module summaries. We evaluate BinXSight on stripped binaries across various sizes, fields, platforms, and architectures. Results show that BinXSight outperforms baselines by 23.18% to 46.99%, and summarizes a binary with about 3K functions in 24.3 seconds on average. In addition, a user study with 27 experts shows that BinXSight's high-quality summaries help users quickly understand the whole binary. Our case analysis on recent real-world malware further demonstrates its practical utility.

authors.name: Zhipeng Gao
authors.institution: Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications

papers.title: Weighted sum commuting maps with the $(f,g)$-Aluthge transform
papers.abstract: Let $\mathbb{M}_n(\mathbb{C})$ denote the algebra of all $n\times n$ complex matrices, where $n\geq2$, and let $\Delta_{f,g}$ be the $(f,g)$-Aluthge transform associated with nonnegative continuous functions $f,g$ on $[0,\infty)$ satisfying $f(t)g(t)=t$ for all $t\geq0$. In this paper, we characterize all surjective maps $\Phi:\mathbb{M}_n(\mathbb{C}) \to\mathbb{M}_n(\mathbb{C})$ satisfying\[\Phi(\Delta_{f,g}(\alpha A+\beta B))=\Delta_{f,g}(\alpha\Phi(A)+\beta\Phi(B))\]for all $A,B\in\mathbb{M}_n(\mathbb{C})$, where $\alpha,\beta$ are fixed nonzero real numbers. Without assuming additivity or linearity, we prove that when $f$ is nonconstant, $\Phi$ must be of the form $\Phi(A)=cUAU^*$ or $\Phi(A)=cU\overline{A}U^*$ for all $A$, where $U$ is a fixed unitary matrix, $\overline{A}$ denotes the entrywise complex conjugate of $A$, and $c$ is a nonzero complex scalar. Moreover, we completely determine the possible values of $|c|$, which form either $\{1\}$, $q^{\mathbb{Z}}$ for some $q>1$, or $(0,\infty)$. When $f$ is constant, we show that $\Phi(A)=S(A)+D$ for all $A$, where $S$ is a surjective $\mathbb{Q}(\alpha,\beta)$-linear map and $D\in\mathbb{M}_n(\mathbb{C})$ satisfies $(\alpha+\beta-1)D=0$.

authors.name: Jing-Bin Zhou
authors.institution: Beijing Chao-Yang Hospital, Capital Medical University

papers.title: Your Camera Can Hear You: Side-Channel Acoustic Eavesdropping via Android Camera2 Metadata
papers.abstract:
To prevent motion sensors from acting as covert microphones, Android 12+ caps SensorManager gyroscope and accelerometer rates at 200 Hz by default, requires HIGH_SAMPLING_RATE_SENSORS for higher rates, and throttles sensors back to 200 Hz when the microphone toggle is off. We show that Android's Camera2 subsystem bypasses these defenses. During an active Camera2 session, Camera HAL stabilization pipelines record high-rate gyroscope measurements and export them via vendor CaptureResult metadata. Loudspeaker speech excites chassis vibrations that couple into this path. Across 50 smartphones (2020-2026) from 10 vendors, 37 expose gyroscope metadata via Camera2, and 26 exceed 200 Hz--including six flagship models at 800-1000 Hz, double SensorManager's 400-500 Hz ceiling. This channel requires neither RECORD_AUDIO nor HIGH_SAMPLING_RATE_SENSORS and defeats privacy switches: turning off the microphone toggle does not throttle metadata, and turning off the camera toggle blanks only video frames while 800-1000 Hz metadata keeps streaming.
  To build a zero-profiling attack that generalizes to unseen phones, we introduce Source-to-Leakage Learning (S2L). Prior attacks train on real sensor traces, entangling speech with a specific phone's mechanical resonances and sampling rate. S2L decouples speech content from hardware acoustics using a physics-constrained forward simulator. Trained exclusively on simulated leakage without target-phone traces, our universal recognizer CamEar achieves 52.1% mean word accuracy (up to 61.8%) and 74.3% character accuracy (up to 80.7%) across the six 800-1000 Hz phones. In contrast, ISpyU models fine-tuned on real target-phone data drop to 25.9% word accuracy on unseen phones; CamEar improves cross-device accuracy by 101.4% and outperforms ISpyU's same-device models on every tested phone.

papers.title: MemOnce: A Scalable Memory Architecture for Large Language Models
papers.abstract: Deploying large language models (LLMs) in long-horizon and continual interactions requires maintaining reusable memory states for future inference, posing challenges for existing architectures. Standard Transformers accumulate layer-wise, token-level KV caches, incurring linear GPU memory growth and quadratic computational complexity as the context expands. In contrast, linear-time architectures compress history into fixed-size states, but struggle to retain fine-grained details. We introduce MemOnce, a foundation architecture that learns scalable memory states for language models. MemOnce is based on two core designs: (a) Memory encoder-decoder: it caches only a small subset of final-layer hidden states as compact memory representations and dynamically decodes them back into KV caches for attention layers; (b) Memory sparse attention: for each continual input, MemOnce adaptively retrieves relevant memory representations, with the sparse indices computed only once across layers. Coupling these two designs enables efficient on-the-fly memory loading and KV cache decoding, drastically reducing the GPU memory footprint and achieving linear-time complexity. We conduct extensive experiments to show that MemOnce outperforms Transformers and other architectures across varying model sizes, context lengths, and training paradigms (pretraining and post-training adaptation). In particular, adapting Qwen3.5-4B with MemOnce reduces memory state cache by 1313$\times$ and prefill latency by 6.9$\times$ at 1M context, and improves throughput by 3.5$\times$ and overall memory performance by +5.77%. Finally, MemOnce generalizes zero-shot to downstream representation tasks, achieving competitive results against specialized models.

papers.title: Computing Weighted Set Covers with Heterogeneous Stochastic Oracles: Deadline-Constrained Token Complexity
papers.abstract:
We study computation in which a probabilistic Turing machine (PTM) uses AI systems, abstracted as heterogeneous stochastic oracles (HSOs), to solve Weighted Set Cover. A pilot study shows that an LLM can outperform weighted greedy. HSOs differ in capabilities, response distributions, latencies, and token costs. We study how the PTM selects HSOs to obtain, by a deadline and with a required success probability, a full cover satisfying a prescribed weight threshold, and we analyze expected token cost.
  For queries requesting full covers, assuming independent call successes and uninformative failures, we characterize by linear programming the minimum expected token cost for every feasible success probability. An optimal policy randomizes over at most two preselected sequences of oracle batches. Among policies attaining maximum success probability, the expected cost reduction of two-batch selection relative to querying all oracles in one batch is nonnegative and submodular. We construct an FPTAS for near-optimal cost reduction under heterogeneous response-time bounds. Computing an optimal two-batch selection is NP-hard but admits a pseudopolynomial algorithm for positive integral expected token costs.
  For partial-cover responses, the PTM combines returned sets across batches and turns. Once their union covers the universe, it verifies total weight directly or obtains a guarantee from LP-dual tests on retained partial covers. We give one-turn probability, token-cost, and hardness results and adaptive token-cost bounds under per-batch assumptions. A constructed instance shows that residual-guided querying can reduce expected token cost by a factor linear in the number of possible residual subproblems.

papers.title: Dual-Agent DRL based Cooperative Beamforming and Trajectory Optimization for UAV-ISAC Networks
papers.abstract: This paper considers a low-altitude unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) network, where multiple ground base stations (BSs) provide integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) services for multiple communication UAVs (C-UAVs) and sensing UAVs (S-UAVs). With the objective of maximizing the average sum rate of C-UAVs over the entire flight episode, we jointly optimize the multi-BS multi-UAV ISAC beamforming and trajectory design, subject to the BS transmit power budget and the sensing signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio (SINR) constraints of S-UAVs, as well as the flight mission and collision avoidance constraints of C-UAVs and S-UAVs. Based on the multi-agent deep reinforcement learning (MADRL) technique, we develop a dual-agent scheme, termed DeepDA-OPT, to solve the resulting constrained Markov decision process (MDP). In the proposed DeepDA-OPT scheme, two agents, i.e., Agent-B and Agent-T, are specifically deployed for learning the multi-BS ISAC transmit beamformers and the C-UAV/S-UAV trajectories, respectively, where the optimal BS receive beamformers for the sensing echo signals of S-UAVs are obtained in closed form by leveraging the generalized Rayleigh quotient theorem. To mitigate the overestimation of value functions, both Agent-B and Agent-T are trained based on the twin-delayed deep deterministic (TD3) policy-gradient algorithm. In addition, a constraint-aware noise exploration policy is employed, and the reward function is designed to incorporate a sensing penalty and a flight urgency penalty, thereby guiding the training of Agent-B and Agent-T. Numerical results show that, compared with the baseline schemes, the proposed DeepDA-OPT scheme achieves a higher average sum rate of C-UAVs, while the sensing SINR constraints are empirically well satisfied and no collision violation is observed under the evaluated settings.

authors.name: Kaijian Yang
authors.institution: Chongqing University of Posts and Telecommunications

authors.name: Feng Wang
authors.institution: Harbin University of Science and Technology

papers.title: PAVE: A Harness for Geometrically Consistent Road Network Modeling with Vision-Language Models
papers.abstract: Transportation models, whether they simulate traffic or support planning, are only as reliable as the road networks they run on, down to the lanes and turns at each intersection. Practitioners still take such a network from GIS files and supply its junction and movement data by hand, a task that recurs with each new base year and design alternative, or they generate it from open map data. OpenStreetMap's lane tags give the correct layout for only 13 of the 44 approaches we test; open map data are often incomplete or inaccurate. Satellite and street-level imagery, in contrast, cover all 44 and show their lanes as painted. Vision-language models (VLMs) can read such imagery, but asked directly they lose geometric consistency when the same lane must be matched across a satellite crop, street-level photos taken from different poses and an ID-labelled network. We therefore present PAVE (Perceive, Anchor, Verify, Edit), a harness in which code measures what can be measured, traffic engineering knowledge enters as general rules and checks, and the model makes only the open judgements, each anchored to network IDs so that checks catch answers that contradict a measurement, a second reading or a traffic rule. Scored against human labels at signalised intersections, PAVE raises the share of exactly correct lane layouts from 49-64% with a single request to 86-91% for two VLMs, with most of the gain coming from reading one approach at a time on traced lanes. The same division of work edits a real network to a planning brief: the model names the links and nodes of each part of a facility, and code builds the edit from a design template. Of 18 edits, 16 pass every network check, against none when the model writes its own code, and 2 contain a design or coding error, against 7. An analysis shows where VLMs lose geometric consistency and which check catches each failure.

authors.name: Yajun Liu
authors.institution: Harbin University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Coerciveness for complex Hessian type equations
papers.abstract: We study complex Hessian type equations associated with right-Noetherian polynomials on compact K\"ahler manifolds of complex dimension $n$. For two such polynomials of the same degree $2\le d\le n$ in strict proper position, we prove that under the integrability condition and the assumption that the admissible space $\mathcal{H}_2$ is non-empty, smooth admissible solvability for $f_1$, the $d_1$-coerciveness of the associated variational functional $J_1$ on normalized potentials, and the numerical criterion for $f_1$ are equivalent to each other. This extends the existence-coerciveness correspondence of Chen-Ghosh-Wang to the lower-degree setting under weaker polynomial conditions.

authors.name: Junbang Liu
authors.institution: Research Institute of Petroleum Exploration and Development

papers.title: Long-time existence for wave systems with derivative nonlinearities
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study wave systems with power-type derivative nonlinearities in space dimensions $n\geq3$, for small, spherically symmetric initial data. Under suitable assumptions on the nonlinear powers, we establish global existence and sharp lifespan lower bounds. To achieve this, we develop weighted energy and local energy estimates adapted to the null directions, together with corresponding pointwise decay estimates.

papers.title: On the Delandtsheer Conjecture
papers.abstract: We prove the Delandtsheer Conjecture of 1988 that a line-primitive automorphism group of a finite linear space is point-primitive.

papers.title: A Geometric Approach to the Classification of Locally-APN Niho-Type Power Functions
papers.abstract: Let $q=2^m$ with $m\geq 2$. We develop a geometric approach to the classification of locally-APN Niho-type power functions over $\mathbb{F}_{q^2}$. Our approach begins with a characterization of $\mathbb{F}_q$-homogeneous functions: the conditions $D_F(a,F(a))=q$ and $D_F(a,b)\leq 2$ for every $a\in\mathbb{F}_{q^2}^*$ and $b\neq F(a)$ hold if and only if the projective graph of $F$ is a $(q+1)$-arc in $\mathrm{PG}(3,q)$. For Niho-type power functions, this differential condition is equivalent to the locally-APN property. Applying the classification of $(q+1)$-arcs and the description of their stabilizers, we prove, for $m\geq 3$, that $F_s(x)=x^{s(q-1)+1}$ is locally-APN if and only if $s\equiv(2^k+1)^{-1}\pmod{q+1}$ for some $1\leq k\leq 2m-1$ satisfying $\gcd(k,m)=\gcd(2^k+1,q+1)=1$. Together with the known case $m=2$ and the sufficient condition of Xie et al., this gives the complete classification and confirms the conjecture of Cui, Luo, and Xiang.

papers.title: BioCL-POS: Biological Completer-aware Learning with Predictive Observation Selection - A Wild Ginseng Study
papers.abstract: Growers and traders rely on root morphology to assess wild ginseng, yet breakage can obscure important structural traits. We study point cloud completion to provide geometric references for morphological analysis. Does providing more observed points always improve 3D completion? We test whether selected subsets improve recovery of the original missing region while keeping the pretrained completer fixed. We introduce BioCL-POS, an external selector that predicts how the completer responds to candidate inputs. For each candidate, we predict the displacement and distance from shared spatial locations to the nearest points in its completion. We use these spatial responses to estimate recovery quality and supervise them with measurements from actual completions. At inference, we select an input from the observed geometry and run the completer once. We evaluate four frozen completers on controlled gaps in ginseng and tree data at 5%,10%, and 20% omission, and examine 30% omission on ginseng. At 5--20% omission, we outperform full-input completion and all five alternative selectors on both datasets with all four completers. We achieve lower mean reconstruction error and higher mean F-score and coverage. We thus show that selecting observations can improve geometric recovery without retraining the completer, providing more accurate geometric references for subsequent morphological analysis.

authors.name: Taolue Liu
authors.institution: University of Science and Technology of China

papers.title: Balanced Boolean Functions from Sparse Niho-Type Permutation Polynomials: Few-Valued Walsh Spectra and Applications
papers.abstract: We study balanced Boolean functions parameterized by two-to-one mappings of the forms $P(x+x^2)$ and $P(x+x^{-1})$, where $P$ is a sparse permutation polynomial with generalized Niho-type exponents. First, for $q=2^m$ with $m$ even, we determine the complete four-valued Walsh distribution of the balanced Boolean function parameterized by $Q(x+x^2)$, where $Q(x)=x(1+x^{q-1}+x^{2(q-1)})$. We then generalize a permutation polynomial studied by Gupta and Sharma to the parameterized family $P_\lambda(x)=x^{3q-1}+\lambda x^{2q}+\lambda x^2$ over $\mathbb{F}_{q^2}$. We prove that $P_\lambda$ is a permutation polynomial if and only if either $\lambda=0$, or $\lambda\ne0$ and $X^3+X+\lambda^{-1}$ has no root in $\mathbb{F}_q$. Moreover, the number of admissible parameters is $(q+2)/3$ when $m$ is even and $(q+4)/3$ when $m$ is odd. Thus, admissible parameters exist for every $m\geq2$, and approximately one-third of the elements of $\mathbb{F}_q$ yield permutation polynomials. For every admissible parameter $\lambda$, we determine the complete Walsh distribution of the balanced Boolean function $f_\lambda$ parameterized by $P_\lambda(x+x^2)$ and prove that this distribution is independent of $\lambda$. For $m\geq3$, these functions have the five-valued Walsh spectrum ${q,0,-q,-2q,-3q}$, while for $m=2$ the spectrum degenerates to four values. As applications, their supports yield projective minimal binary five-weight codes, sets with five hyperplane intersection numbers, and regular cubelike Cayley graphs with six distinct eigenvalues. Finally, for mappings of the form $P(x+x^{-1})$, we construct an infinite family of balanced Boolean functions with simple explicit trace representations.

papers.title: Independence number, clique number, and maximum degree
papers.abstract: We prove that for every integer $r \ge 3$, every $K_r$-free graph $G$ on $n$ vertices with minimum degree $\delta(G) > (5r-11)n/(5r-5)$ satisfies $\alpha(G) \ge n/(r-1)$. This resolves a conjecture posed by Brandt in 2001 and establishes the sharp minimum-degree threshold for guaranteeing an independent set of size at least $n/(r - 1)$ in $K_r$-free graphs.

authors.name: Xinmin Hou
authors.institution: University of Science and Technology of China

papers.title: A fast automatically adaptive integral equation solver for nonlinear two-point boundary value systems
papers.abstract: We present a fast, high-order, automatically adaptive integral-equation solver for nonlinear two-point boundary value systems. The method builds on the fast direct solver for linear second-kind integral equations and completes the mathematical formulation needed for general boundary conditions, including cases in which the simplest background Green's function is singular and cases with genuinely rank-deficient boundary conditions. Nonlinear problems are written as nonlinear second-kind integral equations and are solved by combining this fast adaptive linear solver with Newton iteration and user-specified continuation. In this way the nonlinear solver inherits the full strengths of the linear integral-equation method: a fast direct solver, arbitrary order accuracy, and automatic adaptive resolution with only a small overhead over a solve on the final mesh. The resulting algorithm is particularly effective for problems with localized or multiscale structure, including boundary layers, dense oscillations, transition regions, hypersensitive optimal-control systems, and singular perturbations. The same framework also provides a computational foundation for future studies of bifurcation and solution-branch exploration.

authors.name: Jun Wang
authors.institution: Harbin University of Science and Technology

papers.title: A Stochastic Tamed-Regularized Random Batch Method for Uncertain Particle Systems with Singularities
papers.abstract: The coefficients of particle systems often exhibit uncertainties due to incomplete knowledge. For particle systems with uncertainties and singularities in the drift and diffusion terms, existing methods may encounter numerical blow-up. In this paper, we propose a novel stochastic tamed-regularized Random Batch (str-RB) method for such uncertain particle systems with singularities. Specifically, since singularities in the diffusion term are more challenging than those in the drift term, building on a tamed scheme, we design an exponential regularization strategy that more effectively mitigates singularities in the diffusion term. This strategy ensures that the stochastic Galerkin (sG) projection coefficients remain finite even when the corresponding integrals for the original singular diffusion coefficient diverge. The sG method is applied to handle the random coefficients, and a random batch approach is then employed to reduce the computational complexity of large-scale simulations. Several theoretical properties of the proposed algorithm are established. Numerical tests demonstrate that the str-RB algorithm exhibits weak convergence, achieves lower errors than major existing methods across singular tests, and remains stable in a wider range of singular regimes. This work provides a robust and accurate approach for uncertain particle systems with singularities, laying a foundation for high-performance solvers in uncertain many-body dynamics.

authors.name: Wenyi Wang
authors.institution: The Affiliated Yongchuan Hospital of Chongqing Medical University

authors.name: Lei Li
authors.institution: Harbin University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Counting cliques in optimal $1$-planar graphs
papers.abstract: Extremal problems concerning the maximum number of cliques in $n$-vertex graphs from a given graph class have been widely investigated. In this contribution, we present several results on counting cliques that extend beyond the existing framework. Firstly, we address this problem for the class of optimal 1-planar graphs where we determine the maximum numbers of copies of $K_3$, $K_4$, and $K_5$ in an $n$-vertex optimal 1-planar graphs and characterize all extremal graphs. This resolves Question {\b 8.1} of Gollin-Hendrey-Methuku-Tompkins-Zhang. Secondly, we prove that every 3-connected plane quadrangulation on $n\geq14$ vertices has at most $2n-14$ 3-separators and characterize the corresponding extremal graphs. This confirms Conjecture {\b 8.2} posed by Gollin-Hendrey-Methuku-Tompkins-Zhang. Lastly, we construct, for every integer $r\geq1$, a simple 2-planar graph with $5r+3$ vertices and $44r+1$ triangles, thus disproving Conjecture {\b 8.3} of theirs. Our proofs use radial graphs, tree decomposition and SPQR trees.

authors.name: Shuchao Li
authors.institution: Harbin University of Science and Technology

papers.title: GaLF-ST: Gaussian Latent Fields for Spatial Transcriptomics Reconstruction
papers.abstract: Spatial transcriptomics (ST) measures gene expression at known tissue locations to reveal tissue organization and cellular function. Expression prediction requires modeling both local spatial relationships and associations among genes. Existing methods typically model expression using coordinate networks without explicit spatial parameterization. To address limited spatial sampling and sparse expression observations of ST, some methods firstly fit intermediate embeddings and then train expression predictors, but a latent representation suited to expression reconstruction may be difficult to predict from spatial coordinates. The two training stages can impose different demands on the latent representation. In this paper, we propose GaLF-ST, a Gaussian latent field method in which learnable Gaussian centers and anisotropic covariances determine the weights of latent vectors at each location. A shared nonlinear decoder maps their weighted average to multigene expression. In GaLF-ST, observed expression error jointly updates the Gaussian geometry, latent vectors, and decoder parameters. We further establish a unified benchmark across seven dataset groups and three held-out fractions, comparing GaLF-ST with four representative methods using the same locations, splits, gene panels, and scoring rules. Across tissues and observation densities, GaLF-ST achieves leading overall reconstruction performance, recovering spatial gene expression patterns and preserving tissue domains from limited observations while substantially reducing runtime and GPU memory usage.

authors.name: Yifan Luo
authors.institution: Wuhan University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Exercised, Rarely Recovered: What Public Reports Say About Recovery in 50 AI Agent Harnesses and Runtimes
papers.abstract: When an AI coding agent deletes the wrong files or a long agent run crashes, users fall back on recovery mechanisms: resume from a checkpoint, undo, ask for approval, read the log. Research runtimes promise stronger guarantees, such as saga-style compensation and transactional rollback. We ask what public evidence shows about whether either kind works in real use. Under a protocol frozen before data collection, we graded 12 persistent agent runtimes, 26 coding-agent harnesses and 12 research runtimes on eight recovery mechanisms, from not found to exercised in a real run, with two blind coding passes, adjudication and re-verification against archived sources. Recovery is exercised almost everywhere in practice: 11 of 12 runtimes and 25 of 26 harnesses have at least one real-use report. Yet of 128 such reports, only 19 describe the run fully recovering; 54 are partial and 45 failed. Checkpoint/resume recovered once in 27 reports, rollback once in 15. Research runtimes show the opposite profile: guarantees evaluated on benchmarks, none reported in operation, and compensation of external effects, their central guarantee, is offered by no harness at all.

papers.title: Integrating Generative Artificial Intelligence with Learning Style Models: Opportunities, Challenges, and Future Directions
papers.abstract: Generative Artificial Intelligence (Generative AI) has emerged as a powerful tool for transforming learning. This review examines how Generative AI can be integrated with established learning style models (VARK, Kolb, Felder-Silverman, and Honey & Mumford) to support student engagement in large online classes. Following PRISMA 2020 guidelines, we searched Scopus, IEEE Xplore, and Google Scholar (2015 to 2026) and included 41 studies that met the eligibility criteria. The review maps Generative AI capabilities to learning style preferences, synthesizes existing implementations, highlights benefits and challenges, and proposes pathways for future research and practice. Despite ongoing debates regarding the empirical validity of learning styles, Generative AI enables flexible, multimodal, and real-time adaptation. This study offers practical insights for educators and developers seeking to build more effective, learner centered learning systems

authors.name: Malithi Nawarathne
authors.institution: Sri Lanka Institute of Information Technology

authors.name: Prasanna Haddela
authors.institution: Sri Lanka Institute of Information Technology

authors.name: Nuwan Kodagoda
authors.institution: Sri Lanka Institute of Information Technology

papers.title: CanopyFormer: Attention-Guided SegFormer for Explainable Forest Cover Segmentation
papers.abstract: In transformer segmentation models, attention is usually visualized after training rather than supervised. Although attention supervision has been explored for natural images and driving scenes, aerial forest segmentation typically uses attention only as an architectural component and evaluates interpretability qualitatively. We present CanopyFormer, an attention-guided SegFormer-B0 that uses an Attention Consistency Loss to align attention with the ground-truth forest mask, encouraging attention to focus on canopy regions. Since SegFormer uses spatial-reduction attention, we adapt Gradient-weighted Attention Rollout by restricting it to the final encoder stage, where the attention matrix is square. We introduce Average Attention-Mask Overlap (AAMO) to measure attention alignment and incorporate a deletion test to evaluate faithfulness. On 5108 images, our method increases AAMO from 0.0334 to 0.7476, approximately 22 times the vanilla SegFormer-B0 result, with a modest decrease in Dice score from 0.8743 to 0.8577. The deletion test reveals that improved alignment does not necessarily translate into improved faithfulness: removing the most-attended 25% of patches reduces the forest score by 12.1%, compared with 33.0% when removing random patches. Attention supervision introduces no additional inference cost, although double backpropagation makes each training step 2.6 to 2.8 times slower. The attention alignment improvement also generalizes to a second dataset, LoveDA. Additionally, a Boundary Refinement Module provides no consistent Dice improvement and reduces AAMO, while mean squared error substantially outperforms Kullback-Leibler divergence as the attention loss.

papers.title: The regular $N$-gon maximizes first positive Neumann eigenvalue among simple polygons with at most $N$ sides and fixed area
papers.abstract: Let $\Phi(P)=|P|\mu_1(P)$, where $\mu_1(P)$ is the first positive Neumann eigenvalue of $P$. For every $N\ge3$, the regular $N$-gon $R_N$ uniquely maximizes $\Phi$, up to congruence, among simple polygons of fixed area with at most $N$ sides. The values $\Phi(R_N)$ increase strictly with $N$. The maximization theorem answers Laugesen's question \cite[Problem~(1), p.~405]{ABLW} and proves the polygonal Szeg\H{o}--Weinberger conjecture of Laugesen and Siudeja \cite[Conjecture~6.36]{LSH}. It also implies that the triangular lattice maximizes the first positive Neumann eigenvalue of the Voronoi cell at fixed covolume.

papers.title: M\"obius expansion and pointwise energy transfer over arbitrary fields
papers.abstract:
Let $F$ be a field of positive characteristic $p$, and let $A\subset F^\times$ have $N$ elements. We prove that, for every $\lambda\in F^\times$, \[
  \card{A+\lambda A^{-1}}\gg\min\{N^{10/9},(pN^2)^{1/3}\}. \] This improves the exponent $31/30$ to $10/9$ in the common small-set range. Over prime fields the bound strengthens to $\min\{N^{10/9},(pN)^{1/2}\}$. Analogous bounds hold for $Af(A)$ when $f$ is a M\"obius transformation satisfying the stated nondegeneracy conditions. In characteristic zero, the bound $N^{10/9}$ remains valid. No subfield-avoidance condition is required.

authors.name: Yao Zhi
authors.institution: State Key Laboratory of Experimental Hematology

papers.title: Dynamic Memory-enhanced Pattern Relevance Prediction for Long-tailed Graph Classification
papers.abstract: Long-tailed graph classification (LTGC) is common in real-world graph datasets, where a few large head graphs provide rich structural information while many smaller tail graphs offer fewer structural cues, making it harder to learn discriminative representations for tail graphs. To address this size-based imbalance, we propose Dynamic Memory-enhanced Pattern Relevance Prediction (DMPRP), which transfers structural patterns from head graphs to tail graphs. Given a graph representation as a query, a dynamic expert memory module inspired by Knowledge-diverse Experts (KDEX) generates a residual vector that augments the original representation. We train the module using co-occurrence triplets sampled from head graphs at the node, rooted subgraph, and random-walk neighborhood levels. Experiments on five graph classification benchmarks show that DMPRP improves tail performance, and ablation studies show that both the expert module and random-walk supervision contribute to these gains. A controlled experiment on PTC further examines pattern transfer when smaller graphs are denser than larger ones. Our code is available at https://anonymous.4open.science/r/DMPRP-73A5.

authors.name: Jiawei Chen
authors.institution: Chongqing University of Posts and Telecommunications

authors.name: Wenjun Wang
authors.institution: State Key Laboratory of Oncogene and Related Genes

papers.title: The categorical graph minor conjecture and matching complexes
papers.abstract: In the graph minor category $\mathcal G$ of Miyata, Proudfoot and Ramos, the morphisms are the ways of obtaining one connected graph from another by deleting and contracting edges. The categorical graph minor conjecture asserts that every submodule of a finitely generated $\mathcal G^{\mathrm{op}}$-module is finitely generated; it is known for graphs of bounded first Betti number. We disprove this conjecture: it fails for the module assigning to each graph the free module on its spanning trees, which is generated by one element. A quotient of this module has unbounded torsion. We prove, however, that the conjecture holds for all modules depending on a minor morphism only through the induced injection of edge sets. This applies to matching complexes. Let $M_d(G)$ be the complex of edge sets of $G$ spanning subgraphs of maximum degree at most $d$. We prove that the $\mathcal G^{\mathrm{op}}$-module $G\mapsto H_i(M_d(G);\mathbb Z)$ is finitely generated for all $i$ and $d$, which for $d=1$ confirms a conjecture recorded by Ramos, and that a positive integer depending only on $i$ annihilates the torsion of all these groups. The proofs combine Robertson and Seymour's labelled graph minor theorem with a new criterion: if a category has a faithful functor to finite sets and injections and, for every finite set of colours, its objects with coloured underlying sets are well-quasi-ordered by colour-preserving morphisms, then its representations over a left-Noetherian ring form a locally Noetherian category. Unlike the Gr\"obner method of Sam and Snowden, this criterion requires no ordering compatible with the morphisms.

papers.title: On the AF embedding problem
papers.abstract: This article gives a survey of the AF-embedding problem for $C^*$-algebras. The problem asks when a given $C^*$-algebra $A$ embeds into an \emph{approximately finite dimensional} (AF) $C^*$-algebra (a direct limit of finite dimensional $C^*$-algebras). This is largely based on my paper ``Subalgebras of simple AF algebras,'' which shows that separable, exact $C^*$-algebras satisfying the UCT and admitting a faithful, quasidiagonal trace embed into a unital, simple AF algebra. Some other results are also discussed.

papers.title: Adding One More Agent: How AI Team Size and Formation Shape Productivity and Diversity in Human-AI Brainstorming Teams
papers.abstract: Generative AI has improved individual productivity, but whether adding a plurality of AI partners helps or hurts remains open. We crossed AI partnership (one versus two) with behavioral formation (calibrated to average human behavior versus customized by the participant) in a brainstorming experiment ($N$=168) with human-human dyads as reference. Two-AI rooms posted more ideas to the shared board, but human-authored ideas dropped substantially. With one AI partner, formation mattered: humans paired with an average-calibrated AI posted more than any other condition. With two, this effect vanished. Humans continued talking but converted fewer ideas into board posts. AI social talk predicted more human posts, while AI posting volume predicted fewer. AI presence increased global diversity of human-authored ideas, but only a second AI increased within-session differentiation. The number of AI partners and their formation can reshape what the human contributes; single-agent results do not generalize to multi-agent teams.

authors.name: Hao-Chuan Wang
authors.institution: Changchun University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Rethinking Full-Weight LoRA with Domain and Task Adapter Scaling for Question Answering over Portuguese Well Drilling Reports
papers.abstract: Adapting large language models (LLMs) to specialized domains remains challenging, particularly for technical documents such as Portuguese well drilling reports, where annotated data are scarce and domain adaptation may compromise instruction-following capabilities. Although Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) is widely used for parameter-efficient adaptation, its scaling after training remains insufficiently explored. This study investigates the impact of LoRA adapter scaling on question answering over Portuguese drilling reports using Qwen2.5-7B and Llama-3.1-8B. Domain-adaptive pretraining (DAPT) is performed either directly on instruction-tuned models or on their base counterparts, with subsequent adapter transfer, while task-specific adapters are trained on WellQuest, an open-source question-answering dataset derived from Portuguese drilling reports. The two adapters are also combined using complementary weights. Scaling factors ranging from 0.1 to 1.0 are evaluated across multiple training checkpoints using BERTScore. Results show that fractional scaling consistently improves DAPT performance over full-weight application, increasing F1 from 68.8\% to 71.9\% for Qwen2.5-7B and from 63.2\% to 68.5\% for Llama-3.1-8B. QA adapters perform best at high but fractional weights, while base-to-instruct transfer yields better results than direct DAPT on instruct-tuned models. Adapter merging provides a modest improvement for Llama-3.1-8B. Overall, these findings demonstrate that post-training adapter scaling can improve domain adaptation without additional data or training.

authors.name: Wallace Casaca
authors.institution: Centro de Ciências Matemáticas Aplicadas à Indústria

authors.name: Lucas C. Ribas
authors.institution: Instituto de Biociências, Letras e Ciências Exatas, câmpus de São José do Rio Preto

papers.title: A Combinatorial Construction of Symmetric Magic Squares of Order Four
papers.abstract: We construct all symmetric nonnegative integer matrices of order four having a common sum on every row, column, and both diagonals. The construction is a disjoint union of twelve translates of free submonoids, each with five uniquely determined nonnegative integer parameters.Twelve is the smallest possible number of classes among finite disjoint unions of translates of free submonoids generated by five elements, even when generators outside the Hilbert basis are allowed. A comparison-based case analysis supplies integer inverse formulas and assigns every point on the shared faces to exactly one class. The normal forms prove that the twelve primitive extreme-ray generators form the entire Hilbert basis: eight have magic sum two and four have magic sum four. We exhibit the underlying regular unimodular triangulation and a single perturbation direction producing all half-open boundary conventions. The resulting positive multivariate generating function specializes to an explicit rational function and a quasipolynomial of period four in the magic sum. A further consequence is a reflexive lattice polytope associated with positive symmetric magic squares.

papers.title: On the Laugesen--Siudeja Conjecture: A Sharp Lower Bound and Failure of the Upper Bound
papers.abstract: We prove the sharp lower bound in the Laugesen--Siudeja conjecture and give a counterexample to its upper bound. For every bounded convex planar domain, the first Dirichlet eigenvalue $\lambda_1$, the area $A$, and the centroidal polar moment of inertia $I$ satisfy $\lambda_1A^3/I>9\pi^2/2$. The constant is approached by thin isosceles triangles. The lower bound follows from a rectangle comparison in the principal directions of the covariance matrix and a planar random-triangle inequality. For the upper bound, we exhibit an isosceles trapezoid on which $\lambda_1A^3/I>12\pi^2$, using Temple's inequality and exact arithmetic.

papers.title: A Higher-Dimensional Extension of the Laugesen--Siudeja Lower Bound
papers.abstract: We prove a higher-dimensional analogue of the lower bound in the Laugesen--Siudeja conjecture, using a covariance normalization of the first Dirichlet eigenvalue. We give a covariance-dependent lower bound for every bounded convex domain. From this bound we obtain the optimal constant for convex planar domains and for simplices in every dimension \(d\geq2\). If the simplex covariance inequality stated in a 2026 preprint holds, the same constant is optimal over all bounded convex domains in dimensions \(d\geq3\). In each of these cases, the infimum is approached by compressing a regular simplex in the direction of an edge and is unattained.

papers.title: Recovering buoyancy-glitch parameters in low-luminosity red giants from global stellar properties with machine learning
papers.abstract: Buoyancy glitches in red giants provide localized information on the interior structure near the base of the convective envelope, but their properties are typically inferred from dedicated seismic modelling rather than global properties, limiting large-sample applications. We investigate whether the buoyancy-glitch amplitude ($A_g$), location ($W_{\rm g}^{\star}$), and width ($D_g$) can be recovered from global stellar properties using gradient-boosted tree regressors (XGBoost and LightGBM). The models were trained on a grid of 12580 synthetic stellar models of low-luminosity red giants, with target parameters derived from fits to the local buoyancy frequency profile. We find that $W_{\rm g}^{\star}$ and $D_g$ exhibit excellent recoverability, achieving test-set $\mathcal{R}^2$ values of 0.98 and 0.97, respectively. In contrast, $A_g$ shows moderate recoverability overall ($\mathcal{R}^2=0.68$). This reduced recoverability of $A_g$ is concentrated in the large frequency separation range $\Delta\nu = 4.6$--$18.9\,\mu$Hz, where the glitch resides in the evanescent-zone transition between the convective envelope and the gravity-mode cavity, increasing intrinsic scatter. SHAP analysis shows that $\nu_{\rm max}$ and $T_{\rm eff}$ dominate the predictions across all targets, indicating that the regressors rely primarily on evolutionary state. While $W_{\rm g}^{\star}$ and $D_g$ are tightly constrained by global evolutionary trends, the lower recoverability of $A_g$ reflects localized structural complexity associated with red-giant evolution.
